papers.abstract: We propose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) finite element method to approximate the solution of the time-dependent Keller-Segel model, a drift-diffusion system describing chemotactic cell movement. We develop and analyze the corresponding HDG scheme, and establish theoretical convergence results for the proposed discretization. Finally, we present numerical experiments that confirm the theoretical findings.

papers.title: $L^\infty$ blow-up in the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation
papers.abstract: We investigate the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation $$ u_{tttt}+αu_{ttt}+βu_{tt}-γΔu_{tt}-δΔu_{t}-\varrho Δu=(f(u))_{ttt}+(f(u))_{tt} $$ under homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions in a smooth bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\leq 3$, where $α\in \mathbb{R}$ and $β,γ,δ,\varrho>0$. First, for any suitably regular initial data and assuming that $f\in C^4(\mathbb{R})$ with $f(0)=0$, we prove that the corresponding initial-boundary value problem admits a unique maximal strong solution $u$ on $(0, T_{max})$. Second, by combining three time-integrated formulations with a series of resolvent-regularized energy estimates, we show that gradient blow-up is ruled out in the sense that \begin{equation} \tag{*} T_{max}<\infty \quad\,\, \Rightarrow\quad\,\, \limsup_{t\nearrow T_{max}}\|u(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(Ω)}=\infty. \end{equation} Finally, assuming in addition that $f$ is convex and grows superlinearly in the sense that $$ f''(ξ)\geq 0 \;\; \mbox{ for all}\;\;ξ\in\mathbb{R}, \qquad \frac{f(ξ)}ξ\rightarrow +\infty\;\;\mbox{ as}\;\; ξ\rightarrow +\infty , \qquad \int_{ξ_{0}}^{\infty}\frac{dξ}{f(ξ)}<\infty \;\; \mbox{ for some}\;\; ξ_{0}>0, $$ we employ the extensibility criterion (*) to prove that, for a suitable class of initial data, the solution blows up in finite time in the $L^\infty$-norm. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous description of finite-time blow-up for a genuinely nonlinear equation of fourth order in time.

papers.title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
papers.abstract: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollobás and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Gutiérrez, Bernués, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollobás and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.

papers.title: A complete Kähler metric on $\mathbb{C}^n$ of nonnegative Ricci curvature with Euclidean volume growth and nonunique asymptotic cone
papers.abstract: We construct complete smooth Kähler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^n$ , $n\ge2$, with nonnegative Ricci curvature, Euclidean volume growth, and nonunique tangent cones at infinity. More generally, we prescribe the entire tangent cone set within a class of smooth Hopf cones, using a compact connected family of positive transverse Ricci forms on $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. We identify all metric blow-downs and their Ricci currents, compute the exact asymptotic volume ratio, and classify isometries between the model cones. In particular, the Kähler condition does not ensure uniqueness at infinity under nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth, even in complex dimension two.

papers.title: Nonlocal Equations on Domains and Manifolds Without Symmetries
papers.abstract: In this work, we establish existence and regularity results for solutions to nonlinear nonlocal equations of the form $f(Δ)u = U(x,u)$ and $f(Δ_{g})u = U(x,u)$ in Euclidean and Riemannian settings, respectively. We prove existence results across three distinct geometric scenarios: bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, perturbed equations on compact Riemannian manifolds, and noncompact Cartan-Hadamard manifolds under suitable geometric curvature conditions.

papers.title: Reverse Module Categories of Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: We study the realization of the reverse braided category of the module category of a rational vertex operator algebra V. Using holomorphic extensions and commutant constructions, we prove that this realization property is preserved under suitable cosets, tensor products, extensions, and finite-group orbifolds. As applications, we establish the property for unitary Virasoro minimal models, affine vertex operator algebras of types ABCDE at positive integral levels, the corresponding principal W-algebras of type ADE, and related parafermion vertex operator algebras.

papers.title: Energy Estimate and Convergence of Weak Solutions of a Class of Nonlinear PDEs with Robin Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: We establish strong convergence in $L^2([0,T]\times[0,1])$ of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear PDEs with Robin boundary conditions to weak solutions of the corresponding Neumann and Dirichlet problems as the boundary parameter $κ$ tends to $0$ and $\infty$, respectively. Our approach relies on a particle system whose hydrodynamic limits yield the Robin problem for each fixed $κ>0$. An energy estimate derived from the microscopic stochastic dynamics provides the key bounds for passing to the subsequent limits $κ\to0$ and $κ\to\infty$, thereby obtaining the Neumann and Dirichlet problems.

papers.title: Bulk universality of scaling limits for the almost Hermitian Coulomb gas
papers.abstract: Inspired by the recent approach to edge universality of Cronvall and Wennman, we prove several local universality results for scaling limits in the bulk in the almost Hermitian regime, as well as associated results relating to reproducing kernel spaces of the Fock type.

papers.title: Sharp Capacity Estimates and Volume Growth for Fractional Sobolev Spaces
papers.abstract: We obtain sharp two-sided estimates for the relative capacity of fat and thin annuli in the fractional Sobolev spaces $W^s_{p,q}$, where $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(0,\infty)$, $q\in(0,\infty]$, in terms of an explicit volume growth quantity. The underlying space is a general metric measure space equipped with a doubling and reverse doubling measure. In particular, whenever the capacity is finite, the estimates are independent of the parameter $q$, and in the Ahlfors regular case with $p=q$ they recover Costea's logarithmic law at $sp=Q$. For $p<q$, we also introduce a sharp condition on the measure that is necessary for the existence of admissible functions in the space $W^s_{p,q}$. For thin annuli $(B_r,B_{r+\varepsilon r})$ under an $η$-annular decay property, we uncover a purely nonlocal phenomenon: for $sp <η$, the capacity remains bounded as $\varepsilon\to 0$, because the limiting competitor $χ_{B_r}$ already has finite energy, while if $sp\geqη$ it blows up as $ \varepsilon\to0$.

papers.title: Semiclassical Band Splitting in the Infinite Chern Band Model
papers.abstract: We study the two lowest Bloch bands of the infinite Chern band model of Tan and Devakul in the semiclassical limit. When the Berry curvature parameter is an odd multiple of $π$, we show that the first two bands are exponentially close and meet at exactly one Dirac point. The proof combines Agmon estimates and WKB approximations for a matrix Schrödinger operator whose lowest potential eigenvalue has two wells. Geometric properties of the Agmon distance allow us to compute the leading tunneling coefficients by the method of stationary phase. We provide numerical computations to illustrate the asymptotic formula and support the conjecture that the two bands remain separated for other values of the Berry curvature parameter.

papers.title: A Half-Constant Upper Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
papers.abstract: Let lambda(n) denote the infimum of -min_x sum_{a in A} cos(ax) over all sets A of n positive integers. While the classical Sidon-difference construction yields lambda(n) <= (1 + o(1))sqrt(n)/2, we construct sets achieving a leading constant of 1/2: lambda(n) <= (1/2)sqrt(n) + O(n^(1/4)sqrt(log n)), establishing limsup_{n->infinity} lambda(n)/sqrt(n) <= 1/2. This construction combines a two-sided Sidon square identity, a Singer difference set, a Fejer-kernel majorant, a parity-biased deletion, and an exact-cardinality probabilistic selection. We also provide an L^4 criterion and a multiplicity bound constraining any construction with a smaller leading constant. In the opposite direction, we incorporate the L^1 norm into Bedert's boundary estimate with an explicit constant, yielding two lower bounds for f_A(x) = sum_{a in A} cos(ax): (1) -min f_A >= cn^(1/4) for every n-element set A subset of [1, Cn]; and (2) (-min f_A)^3 ||f_A||_1^2 >= cn for every n-element set A subset of N. The second bound recovers the 1/5 exponent of Bedert and Shankar and improves it whenever ||f_A||_1 is small relative to -min f_A. Numerical values of the construction are reported up to |A| = 25,440.

papers.title: A Feasible Direction Method with Active-Set Identification for Derivative-Free Optimization
papers.abstract: We propose a model-based trust region method for derivative-free optimization with simulation-based inequality constraints. We are motivated by settings of simulation optimization in which both function evaluations at infeasible points may be unreliable and constraint evaluations are expensive. Our method maintains feasible incumbents and computes steps from a subproblem suitable for a feasible-direction method in order to encourage generation of feasible trial points. To reduce the computational cost of modeling the constraints, we describe an active-set estimation scheme that permits modeling with only a subset of constraints in each subproblem, as opposed to maintaining models of all constraints. We show that every limit point of the incumbents generated by our method is a Fritz-John point, and is additionally a KKT point under the Mangasarian-Fromovitz constraint qualification. Under standard nondegeneracy conditions, the active-set estimate identifies, within finite time, all constraints active at the limit point of the incumbents. Experiments on CUTEst problems show that our method generates feasible trial points more often than a comparable SQP-based approach and is competitive with an appropriate comparator in budgeted settings.

papers.title: Quantum ordinal optimization under a fixed comparison budget
papers.abstract: Ordinal optimization selects designs that are good enough rather than optimal when evaluation is expensive and the budget is small. The alignment probability measures the chance that the selected set contains at least a prescribed number of truly good designs. We formulate quantum ordinal optimization as a class of problems that maximize this probability under a fixed oracle budget. We study exact, coherent pairwise comparisons with one selected design as a first instance, with the budget counted in comparison queries. For every classical comparison budget smaller than the number of designs, we prove that a knockout among uniformly sampled designs attains the optimum. The sample is drawn without replacement and contains one more design than the number of comparisons. For a uniformly random order, the selected design's rank has a polynomial probability law. At the same comparison budget, the maximum quantum degree is at most twice the classical maximum, a factor attained whenever there are more than twice as many designs as comparisons, so a quantum algorithm can realize rank laws that no classical algorithm with the same budget can. We determine the quantum optimum with one comparison for every number of designs and every good-enough set. For selecting the best of n designs, the optimal success probability with one quantum comparison is approximately 3.30/n for large n, compared with 2/n for one classical comparison. When the best design is sought, one quantum comparison gives a higher alignment probability than two classical comparisons whenever there are more than nine designs.

papers.title: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture after OpenAI
papers.abstract: We provide a simplified and more human-friendly version of the proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture recently given by OpenAI.

papers.title: Global solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson equations in the half-space and exterior domains
papers.abstract: We study the initial boundary value problem for the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson equations without damping in the three-dimensional half-space and in smooth exterior domains. The velocity satisfies the no-slip boundary condition, and the electric potential satisfies the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. For small perturbations of a constant state in $H^3$, with a small initial electric field in $L^2$, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The uniform estimates combine density dissipation, tangential and normal derivative estimates, and a modified energy expressed through the Helmholtz projection. In exterior domains, boundary normal coordinates and localized elliptic estimates control the geometric terms. We also obtain algebraic decay in the full energy norm. In the half-space, finite tangential negative Sobolev norms of order $-s$, with $\frac12\leq s<1$, yield the rate $(1+t)^{-s/2}$. In exterior domains, integrable initial density and velocity perturbations yield the same form of estimate for $0<s<\frac14$. The exterior decay proof uses whole-space negative-order estimates for localized variables and the time integrability of the dissipation.

papers.title: Some Remarks on Regular Sequences and Complete Intersections
papers.abstract: We give an ideal in a polynomial ring in three variables, generated by three elements and having height equal to three, but for which no permutation of its generators is a regular sequence. We prove that in a polynomial ring over an infinite field, an ideal of height n generated by n polynomials, always admits a set of n generators, for which any permutation is a regular sequence.

papers.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carathéodory Extension in Net Convergence Groups
papers.abstract: We study extension of additive measures when the range carries a prescribed separated Abelian net convergence. On a $σ$-complete, lattice-$σ$-continuous pseudo-D-lattice, we prove an uncontrolled modular extension theorem using finite-response reflection, closed countable summation and uniform closure. Completeness is imposed only on the limit-stable hull of the source values. No topology, lattice order or positive control is required in its range. Modular interval identities, an order-null separation argument and two uniform transfer arguments construct the extension before establishing its normality. A separate relative lifting theorem combines this modular construction with a nonmodular Sasaki argument. Its cone conditions are verified for positive lattice-group values, lattice-normed groups, products and limit-stable subgroups. These verifications give explicit positive, dominated lattice-normed and topological corollaries. Uniqueness holds among all sigma-additive extensions to the generated domain. Sion's inner and outer nets exist in the original convergence and recover the extension there. For Boolean domains we retain the stronger identification with the full regulated splitting class and the finite-variation and finite-semivariation results.

papers.title: Coanalytic subfields and bases of prescribed dimension
papers.abstract: Assume $V=L$. We prove two uniform theorems producing coanalytic sets of prescribed Hausdorff dimension in Euclidean space. The first concerns countable families of partial operations of finite arity on $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose evaluation is hyperarithmetic and which are tame in each vector variable separately. For such families a single lightface $Π^1_1$ relation yields strictly increasing, left-continuous chains of proper sets closed under the operations, one of each Hausdorff dimension in $[0,n]$, uniformly in the family and in $n$; no exchange property of the closure is needed. As an application, there are coanalytic proper subfields of $\mathbb{R}$ of every Hausdorff dimension in $[0,1]$. The second theorem constructs coanalytic bases of every possible Hausdorff dimension for effectively coded pregeometries. As an application, there are coanalytic Hamel bases of $\mathbb{R}^n$ and transcendence bases of $\mathbb{C}$ of every Hausdorff dimension in $[0,n]$ and $[0,2]$, respectively.

papers.title: Webs and finite dimensional representation theory for quantum symmetric pairs
papers.abstract: We develop a highest weight framework and construct explicit finite dimensional irreducible modules for the type AIII (quasi split) quantum symmetric pair subalgebras $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$. In Part 1, we provide a uniform construction of Cartan subalgebras and Verma modules for both subfamilies. Our construction recovers Letzter's Cartan subalgebra in one subfamily and gives a new Cartan subalgebra in the other. We construct a weak triangular decomposition of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$ via the Letzter map. Then we define Verma modules as induced modules and prove that finite dimensional simple $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$-modules are quotients of our Verma modules. In Part 2, we define a diagrammatic category $Web^B$ that controls polynomial representations of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$. We prove a multiplicity-free decomposition of the quantum exterior powers $\bigwedge^k\mathbb{V}$ as a $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$-module, using a explicit eigenspace decomposition of certain dot morphisms in $Web^B$. As applications, we deduce the multiplicity-freeness of the involved anti-spherical Hecke module. For $\bigwedge^k\mathbb{V}$, we explicitly determine the highest weight vectors and their weights, thereby determining the isomorphism classes of their irreducible summands. Finally, we determine the kernel of the $Web^B$-action on certain finite dimensional representation category of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^θ)$.

papers.title: Radii of Starlikeness of Spirallike Functions
papers.abstract: A normalized analytic function $f$ defined on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ is called $α$-spirallike if $f(\mathbb{D})$ is an $α$-spirallike domain, that is, for every $z\in f(\mathbb{D})$, the $α$-spiral $ze^{-e^{iα}t}$, $t\ge0$, is contained in $f(\mathbb{D})$, or equivalently, if $\operatorname{Re}\!\left(e^{iα} {zf'(z)}/{f(z)}\right)>0$ for all $z\in \mathbb{D}$. The 0-spirallike functions are the usual starlike functions. The function $f$ is parabolic starlike, if $\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\right)>\left|\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}-1\right|$, and lemniscate starlike if $|(zf'(z)/f(z))^2-1|<1$ respectively. In this paper, we determine the radii of parabolic starlikeness and lemniscate starlikeness of $α$-spirallike functions. Our approach combines geometric characterizations of the underlying regions with the resultant method for eliminating auxiliary variables, leading to explicit equations for the sharp radii. Some known radius results are recovered as special cases.

papers.title: Omega bounds for the Piltz divisor problem
papers.abstract: We improve our earlier omega bounds for the error term in the Piltz divisor problem over number fields. Our proof uses a weighted extension of a counting theorem of Balasubramanian and Ramachandra and an extension of Lamzouri's kernel to apply the long resonance method. We also discuss applications of our results to lattice points in norm-form regions, invariant sublattices, abelian covers of curves, spectral counting, and representation growth of Heisenberg groups.

papers.title: Breaking the Infinite Barrier in the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ Conjecture
papers.abstract: The balance constant is a poset parameter measuring how well random linear extensions can be split according to their relative order on two elements. We give an $\varepsilon$-improvement for the balance constant over the bound by Brightwell, Felsner and Trotter (1995), for some small $\varepsilon>0$. This is the first general result towards the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ conjecture in over 30 years.

papers.title: The geometry of solutions to the general sextic
papers.abstract: We study the geometry of the three simplest known formulas for roots of a general sextic polynomial. In contrast with work of Green on the quintic, we show that no "simultaneous uniformization" of the normal forms associated to the solutions exists. This demonstrates an intrinsic qualitative complexity of sextic equations that is not present in quintic equations. Additionally, we give a formula for the roots of a general sextic in terms of Hilbert modular cusp forms and the uniformizing differential equation of the associated Hilbert modular surface.

papers.title: Poincaré's Inequality on Sliding-Window Occupation Count Kernels and the Optimal Normalized Spectral-Gap Constant
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be an irreducible reversible Markov kernel on an $m$-state space $Ω$, and denote its right spectral gap by $\Gap(P) =1-λ_2(P)$. For a stationary trajectory, let $K_t$ be the occupation-count vector of the length-$n$ window beginning at time $t$. The stationary pair $(K_0,K_1)$ defines a reversible projected count kernel $\widetilde P_n$. For each fixed $m\ge2$, define \[ c_m^\star= \inf_{\substack{|Ω|=m,\ P\ \mathrm{irreducible\ and\ reversible} n\ge2}} \frac{n\Gap(\widetilde P_n)}{\Gap(P)}. \] We prove \[ \frac1{1080m}\le c_m^\star\le q_{m-2}, \qquad q_0=\frac14,\quad q_{r+1}=q_r(1-q_r). \] We also show $q_{m-2}=(m+\log m+O(1))^{-1}$, which implies that $c_m^\star=Θ(m^{-1})$. Thus, the reciprocal optimal comparison coefficient $C_m^{\mathrm{opt}}=(c_m^\star)^{-1}$ is of the order $m$. In the two-state case, we determine the exact values $c_2^\star=1/4$ and $C_2^{\mathrm{opt}}=4$. %the exact constants for $m\ge3$ remain open. The lower bound also holds for $n=1$ and is uniform in $P$, including sparse and periodic kernels. The proof combines short-window decorrelation with an averaged anchor-excursion decomposition, a Green-kernel hitting estimate, and a stopped Carleson--Hardy inequality. A nested rare-state construction produces finite $m$-state witnesses whose normalized Rayleigh quotients approach $q_{m-2}$ through an ordered sequence of limits. For every fixed finite irreducible reversible aperiodic kernel on at least two states, $\Gap(\widetilde P_n)=Θ_P(n^{-1})$.

papers.title: Hamming Ideals and Grobner Bases for ISD-like Syndrome Decoding
papers.abstract: We investigate an algebraic approach to the Syndrome Decoding Problem, based on a reformulation of the Hamming weight constraint and its integration with the Information Set Decoding paradigm. We begin with a systematic analysis of the Hamming variety, deriving its defining equations in terms of elementary symmetric functions. Since these equations may have high degree, we exploit convolution identities for elementary symmetric functions, together with factorizations based on Lucas' identity, to derive an equivalent formulation with auxiliary variables and equations of bounded degree. Building on this modeling, we generalize the ISD paradigm through an ISD-like decoding strategy, implemented by the GBDecode algorithm, in which only a subset of an information set is fixed. This approach reduces the size of the combinatorial search space at the cost of solving the associated multivariate nonlinear systems. To handle this algebraic component, we employ the MultiSolve algorithm, which replaces a single Grobner basis computation with a collection of computations on simpler systems, obtained by exhaustively assigning a varying number of indeterminates over the finite field. This provides a tunable balance between combinatorial search and algebraic solving. We evaluate the resulting approach experimentally on instances of the Syndrome Decoding Problem for random binary linear codes, using parameters corresponding to the NIST Security Category 1 parameter set of the Classic McEliece cryptosystem. The experiments assess the feasibility of this combinatorial-algebraic approach and provide insights into the practical behavior of Grobner basis techniques within an ISD-like decoding framework.

papers.title: Sharp Strichartz estimates on the one-dimensional torus
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove the sharp Strichartz estimates for the Schrödinger equation on the one-dimensional torus. More precisely, via obtaining a sharp weak $L^{6}$ estimate with no derivative loss, we obtain sharp $L^{6}$ Strichartz estimate, and sharp no loss $L^{p}$ Strichartz estimate for any $2<p<6$. The latter answers a question by Bourgain \cite{Bourgain93}.

papers.title: Prediction with Five Experts and Geometric Stopping: A Probabilistic Construction and Analytic Verification
papers.abstract: We present a solution of the limiting five-expert prediction problem with geometric stopping, based on stochastic calculus and partial differential equations. If $δ$ is the stopping probability, the minimax expected regret from tied initial scores is $45π^2/(512\sqrt{2δ})+o(δ^{-1/2})$ as $δ\downarrow0$. The adversarial rank control selecting the best and third-best experts maximizes the limiting Hamiltonian at every state. Following the four-expert construction of Bayraktar, Ekren, and Zhang (2020), we represent the value correction as a discounted boundary-local-time expectation for a degenerate obliquely reflected Brownian motion. The hyperbolic systems governing its boundary traces are derived and solved explicitly. To verify the nonlinear Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation, we combine heat-equation minimum principles in equality directions, ODE minimum principles applied to convex combinations of multiple controls, and comparisons across controls. These arguments reduce the 48 regional control inequalities to a few lower-dimensional boundary problems, with the remaining signs established by explicit monotonicity arguments and by factorization of multivariate integral kernels that are positive polynomials in some of their variables. We prove global $C^2$ regularity across both regional interfaces and changes in rank ordering. We also show that the alternating COMB control only attains the limiting Hamiltonian maximum exactly when the two highest scores coincide and the third- and fourth-highest scores coincide.

papers.title: Algebraic and measurable embeddings between square-free right-angled Artin groups
papers.abstract: Let $Γ,Δ$ be finite simplicial graphs, and assume that $Γ$ has no induced squares. We prove that the right-angled Artin group $A(Δ)$ measurably embeds into $A(Γ)$ if and only if $A(Δ)$ embeds as a subgroup in a graph product of free abelian groups over $Γ$. This in turn has a graph-theoretical characterisation which can be checked algorithmically. If additionally $A(Γ)$ and $A(Δ)$ have cohomological dimension equal to two and $A(Γ)$ is not isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}\times F_n$, we get that $A(Δ)$ measurably embeds into $A(Γ)$ if and only if it embeds as a subgroup in $A(Γ)$. Our proof relies on the following algebraic statement. Let $K_1,\dots,K_n$ be a family of pairwise disjoint cliques in the square-free graph $Γ$, and let $g_1,\dots,g_n$ be elements of $A(Γ)$ with respective parabolic supports $A(K_1),\dots,A(K_n)$. Then the subgroup of $A(Γ)$ generated by $g_1,\dots,g_n$ is a right-angled Artin group, where the only relations impose that $g_i$ and $g_j$ commute if $K_i\cup K_j$ is contained in a clique of $Γ$. The same holds true more generally for pairwise disjoint cliques $K_1,\dots,K_n$ in the extension graph $Γ^{\mathrm{ext}}$, up to possibly replacing the elements $g_i$ by powers.

papers.title: A positive version of Miljutin's Theorem
papers.abstract: In this paper we provide a positive version of Miljutin's theorem. Namely, we show that for any uncountable compact metric spaces $K$ and $L$ there exists a positive isomorphism $T:C(K)\longrightarrow C(L)$. Moreover, the inverse of $T$ is a regular operator, and $T$ may be chosen so that $\|T\|_\mathrm{r} \cdot \|T^{-1}\|_\mathrm{r} \leq 9+6\sqrt3$. The method also gives positive versions of classical nonmetrizable results for Miljutin and Dugundji compacta. In particular, if $G$ and $H$ are infinite compact groups of the same weight, then $C(G)$ and $C(H)$ are positively and regularly isomorphic with the same uniform quantitative estimate.

papers.title: MOE-DGSCND: Multi-Objective Enterprise Green Supply Chain Network Design
papers.abstract: This paper introduces and studies the Multi-Objective Enterprise Doubly-Green Supply Chain Network Design (MOE-DGSCND) problem, an extension of Multi-Objective Supply Chain Network Design. The problem studied here is a three-objective combinatorial optimization problem that simultaneously minimizes total cost f1, carbon dioxide emissions f2 and customer dissatisfaction f3 over binary decisions regarding which distribution centers to open and how to assign customer zones to open facilities. The problem generalizes the capacitated facility location problem (CFLP) and is known to be NP-hard (Garey and Johnson, 1979). This paper formally specifies the decision variables, objective functions and constraints and investigates three solution approaches using a single numerical instance: (A) an exact weighted-sum integer linear programming (ILP) formulation solved with Python combinatorially and via PuLP, (B) three Fully Polynomial-Time Approximation Schemes (FPTAS) providing (1 + $ε$)-approximate solutions for $ε$ := 0.15 and (C) two baseline heuristics for comparison. On an instance with eight customers and five candidate distribution centers, the exact solver certifies the optimal (sampled) supported solutions across eight weight combinations, while the FPTAS-based approaches complete within milliseconds, compared to centiseconds for the exact ILP on this tiny non-stochastic instance.

papers.title: Convexity of a ratio function involving polygamma functions and monotonicity of the sectional curvature of the Fisher--Rao manifold
papers.abstract: This paper proves that the sectional curvature of the Fisher--Rao manifold of beta distributions, restricted to the diagonal, is strictly decreasing. The proof is based on a general convexity lemma for ratios involving positive decreasing functions and is applied to a quotient of polygamma functions.

papers.title: Quantum lower bounds for convex optimization and real matrix-vector query problems
papers.abstract: We (the author and the AI systems that did the heavy lifting) show that the quantum query complexity of minimizing a convex function over a convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with evaluation and membership queries is $\tildeΩ(n)$, nearly matching the best known upper bound. In particular, we show this even for quadratic minimization, which is equivalent to inverting an $n \times n$ real matrix using matrix-vector queries. We also show linear or nearly linear lower bounds on the quantum query complexity of computing the trace, the sign of the determinant, and the magnitude of the determinant of a real matrix in the matrix-vector query model. We use a novel quantum lower bound technique, the determinantal witness method, based on identifying a witness whose Fourier transform vanishes on low-rank matrices and that correlates well with the function being computed.

papers.title: Categorification in Representation Theory
papers.abstract: In this survey article, we give an introduction to the relatively young subject of $2$-representation theory, which studies categorifications of important players in classical representation theory. In particular, we provide a streamlined exposition of the main results leading to the classification of simple $2$-representations for Soergel bimodules associated to finite Weyl groups in characteristic $0$, obtained in [M. Mackaay, V. Mazorchuk, V. Miemietz, D. Tubbenhauer and X. Zhang, Simple transitive $2$-representations of Soergel bimodules for finite Coxeter types. Proc. London Math. Soc. 126 (2023)].

papers.title: Lie methods for countably categorical Engel groups: the Wilson conjecture for 4-Engel 5-groups
papers.abstract: We are interested in the following conjecture of Wilson from 1981: every locally nilpotent countably categorical group is nilpotent. Following our previous work on the Lie algebra analogue of the conjecture, we use Lie methods to deduce the first nontrivial cases of the Wilson conjecture for n-Engel groups: countably categorical 3-Engel groups and 4-Engel 5-groups are nilpotent, from which we also conclude that countably categorical 4-Engel groups of odd exponent are nilpotent. This is implemented via an exceptional case of the Lazard correspondence, checked using computer algebra systems. We also study the transfer of nilpotency results between the three categories: groups, Lie algebras, associative algebras. Among other things, we prove that the Wilson conjecture implies the analogous nilpotency statement for associative algebras (modulo the commutative case).

papers.title: From Barren Plateaus to SPSA Optimization in Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
papers.abstract: The barren plateau (BP) phenomenon poses a fundamental challenge to the trainability of variational quantum eigensolvers (VQEs) by causing exponentially vanishing gradients as the system size increases. While extensive studies have investigated the geometric origins of BP, its impact on the optimization dynamics and complexity of practical algorithms under finite-shot measurements has received comparatively less attention. In this paper, we develop a theoretical framework that characterizes how the BP affects the optimization dynamics of the Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation (SPSA) algorithm and quantifies the resulting iteration complexity and measurement budget. We derive non-asymptotic bias and variance bounds for the SPSA gradient estimator, introduce a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) defined as the ratio of the gradient energy to the mean squared error of the estimator, and establish convergence guarantees for SPSA under finite-shot measurements. Our results show that, under the proposed parameter schedules, the number of iterations sufficient to guarantee a fixed relative first-order stationarity level scales polynomially with the inverse of the intrinsic gradient energy. Consequently, when this energy decays exponentially under BP, the resulting guaranteed iteration complexity and total measurement budget both grow exponentially with the number of qubits.

papers.title: The determinant of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a surface with boundary and periods of holomorphic differentials on its double
papers.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth orientable $2d$ Riemannian manifold of genus $\mathfrak{g}$ with Riemannian metric $g$ and connected boundary $Γ$. Let $Λ$ be the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on $Γ$ and let ${\rm det}_ζ(Λ)$ be its (modified, i. e. with zero mode excluded) $ζ$-regularized determinant. It is well-known that the quantity ${\rm det}_ζ(Λ)/|Γ|$ (where $|Γ|$ is the length of $Γ$) is a conformal invariant. It was shown by Edward and Wu (\cite{EV}) that this invariant equals one for $\mathfrak{g}=0$; in the case $\mathfrak{g}>0$ Guillarmou and Guillopé \cite{Guillarmou} found two explicit expressions for this invariant through the Rouelle and (respectively) the Selberg zeta-functions of the two surfaces of negative constant curvature from the conformal class of $(M,g)$: one is of infinite volume and complete whereas another has geodesic boundary. We present an elementary counterpart of the formulae of Guillarmou and Guillopé using the periods of holomorphic differentials on the double $2M$ of $M$ only. Our approach is based on the properties of the Hilbert transform of $M$ \cite{B,HilbKor} and the Kontsevich-Vishik-Friedlander-Guillemin regularization of the determinants of pseudodifferenial operators \cite{KV,Ww,F}. In particular, a connection between the length spectra of (uniformized) $M$, $2M$ and the periods of holomorphic differentials on $2M$ is established.

papers.title: Classification of anomalous actions of finite groups with the Rokhlin property
papers.abstract: Given a finite group G, we develop a generalization of the fundamental classification of Rokhlin G-actions on C*-algebras to the setting of anomalous G-actions with the Rokhlin property. For Rokhlin G-kernels on C*-algebras covered by the classification program, this implies that the induced G-action on some known invariants determines the conjugacy class. Extending a result of Izumi, we show that G-kernels with the Rokhlin property on Kirchberg algebras are classified by their anomaly and the induced module structure on the K-theory groups. We explore K-theoretic obstructions for the existence of Rokhlin G-kernels on general separable C*-algebras and use these to characterise which G-module structures arise as K-groups of Kirchberg algebras admitting a Rokhlin G-kernel with a given lifting obstruction.

papers.title: A further study of quandles and quandle rings
papers.abstract: We investigate core quandles and idempotents in quandle rings of core quandles. We answer several questions on the rank of core quandles and nontrivial idempotents in quandle rings. We also present solutions to two questions raised in a recent paper about non-trivial idempotents in quandle rings $\mathbb{Z}[R_5]$ and $\mathbb{Z}[C_5]$, where $\mathbb{Z}$, $R_5$ and $C_5$ are the ring of integers, the dihedral quandle of order 5, and the commutative quandle of order 5, respectively. We then study units in extended quandle rings of a trivial quandle and the Joyce quandle, and nilpotent elements in extended quandles rings of a trivial quandle, where the ground ring is an integral domain. As a consequence, we show that the quandle ring and the extended quandle ring of a trivial quandle are not nil clean rings. We also explore prime rings and semi-prime rings among quandle rings. We introduce zero-divisor graphs of quandle rings and find an intriguing mirror symmetry among the in-degree and out-degree of the vertices. Moreover, we find a bivariate polynomial in the ring $(\mathbb{Z}_{2n+1}[Q])[X,Y]$ that determines the commutative quandle of order $2n+1$, where $2n+1$ is prime.

papers.title: $L^p$ approximation results for infinite dimensional Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Leveraging the neural architectures which we introduced in arXiv:2109.13512v4, we show a global universal approximation theorem in the topology of $L^p(μ)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $μ$ is a Radon probability measure on a suitable infinite dimensional topological space $\mathfrak X$. Namely, any function $f:\mathfrak X\to \mathbb R$ in $L^p(μ)$ can be approximated to any degree of accuracy by suitable infinite dimensional architectures. These architectures can be in turn approximated by almost classical neural networks which are specified by a finite number of parameters only. The vectorial case (where $f=f(x)\in E$ and $E$ is a Banach space) is also considered and analogous results are obtained.

papers.title: On colorful Helly numbers and the growth of Tverberg numbers
papers.abstract: We establish new bounds on colorful Helly and Tverberg numbers in abstract convexity spaces with Radon number $r$. We show that the colorful Helly number is at most $(r-1)2^r$, improving Holmsen--Lee's bound $r^{r^{O(\log r)}}$ and matching the known lower bound $2^{r-1}-1$ up to a factor $O(r)$. Furthermore, we prove that the Tverberg number is $r_k=O(r^{\lceil \log_2 r\rceil }k)$, reducing Pálvölgyi's coefficient $r^{r^{r^{O(\log r)}}}$ to a quasipolynomial function of $r$. For $S_4$-separable spaces, we prove $r_k=O(r^2k)$. In the other direction, we construct a sequence of $S_4$-separable spaces with Tverberg number $r_k=Ω(r^2k)$. This shows that the weak Eckhoff conjecture, asserting that $r_k=O(rk)$ in any abstract convexity space, fails already in separable spaces. The same construction refutes the analogue of Reay's conjecture in separable spaces.

papers.title: A Hopf algebra on permutations with a coupling product
papers.abstract: We define a coupling product and a draw coproduct on permutations and show that they define a graded, connected, cocommutative, free Hopf algebra $\mathbb{KS}$. In characteristic zero, this implies that $\mathbb{KS}$ is isomorphic to a certain cocommutative Hopf algebra associated with the dual of the coradical filtration of the Malvenuto--Reutenauer Hopf algebra on permutations. The coupling product and draw coproduct are permutation analogues of the product and coproduct on the monomial basis of symmetric functions; therefore, we can say that our presentation is a monomial basis for $\mathbb{KS}$.

papers.title: Multiplier obstructions for Legendre pairs of length 333
papers.abstract: A Legendre pair of length 333 would yield a Hadamard matrix of order 668, the smallest order presently unresolved by the Hadamard conjecture. We study the structured case in which both sequences are fixed by a common subgroup $H\leq(\mathbb Z/333\mathbb Z)^\times$ acting by coordinate multiplication. We prove that such a pair can exist only when $|H|\leq 6$. After a mod-3 compression reduces the problem to an order-108 kernel, there are exactly 30 subgroups. We exclude 21 of them, including all 19 subgroups of order at least 9. The final order-9 subgroup is eliminated analytically: its orbit structure restricts the 9-compressed entries to $\{\pm1,\pm17,\pm19,\pm35,\pm37\}$; the Legendre equations force a $+17,-17$ pair in one compressed sequence, and a single-shift autocorrelation bound then contradicts the required compressed correlation. The remaining exclusions use full-image compression, a row-sum congruence, exact meet-in-the-middle enumeration, and proof-carrying pseudo-Boolean encodings. The solver-assisted cases are accompanied by independently checked DRAT proofs or direct arithmetic certificates. The result constrains fixed common-multiplier symmetry only; the unrestricted existence problems remain open.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

papers.title: Free energy and spectral edge of the SYK model
papers.abstract: Consider the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model with $N$ Majorana fermions and interaction order $q$. For even $4\leq q\ll \sqrt{N}$, we present a microscopic framework that determines the free energy limit at every fixed inverse temperature $β>0$. In particular, this gives the first rigorous derivation of the Schwinger-Dyson thermodynamics of the model. For all even $q\in \{4,6,...,N-4\}$, we further determine the asymptotic location of the largest eigenvalue, which answers a question posed by Feng-Tian-Wei \cite{FengTianWei1}. Consequently, we obtained the free energy limit along every sequence $β\equiv β_N\to\infty$.

papers.title: Obstructions to embedding singular curves in toric varieties
papers.abstract: For every integer $d \geq 2$, we show that there exists an irreducible, reduced curve which embeds in $\mathbb{P}^d$ but in no projective normal toric variety of dimension less than $d$. In particular, there exist reduced irreducible curves that embed in $\mathbb{P}^d$ but do not embed in any weighted projective space of dimension less than $d$.

papers.title: On dualizability and invertibility in the higher Morita category
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Lurie characterizing $(n+1)$-dualizability in higher Morita categories of $\mathbb{E}_n$-algebras in terms of dualizability over certain factorization homologies. A key ingredient is a higher Morita category based on the recently developed framework of pointless factorization algebras of Karlsson and the first author. We also verify an invertibility conjecture of Brochier--Jordan--Safranov--Snyder as an immediate corollary of our main result. Moreover, we prove a relative version of the dualizability conjecture, yielding a new criterion for relative/twisted field theories. We give some examples, including Dirichlet and Neumann relative theories.

papers.title: A family of mixed-mixed strongly conservative finite element methods for Biot's model of consolidation
papers.abstract: We consider a four-field formulation of Biot's quasi-static model of consolidation with the (effective) elastic stress, the solid displacement, the fluid flux and the fluid pressure as unknown physical quantities of interest. The weak form of this system composed of the momentum and mass balance equations complemented by the stress-strain relation and Darcy's law yields a two-fold perturbed saddle-point problem. Its well-posedness is proven for a natural choice of inifinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, where the displacement-flux pair is sought in a novel Hilbert space. Next, based on recent works on $H(\rm div \, \rm div)$-conforming finite elements, we propose a family of mixed-mixed finite element methods that preserve the angular momentum as well as the fluid mass balance pointwise, i.e., in a strong sense. We prove the well-posedness of the arising discrete problem and establish optimal a priori error estimates for the related family of fully conservative mixed-mixed finite element methods.

papers.title: On the Role of Normalization in Binary Iterative Hard Thresholding for 1-bit Compressed Sensing
papers.abstract: Binary Iterative Hard Thresholding (BIHT) is a simple, yet effective, greedy method for recovering a sparse vector from one-bit sign measurements. In its original form, BIHT performs a ``gradient-descent'' step, followed by hard thresholding. A convergence analysis of this algorithm was left open in the introductory work of Jacques, Laska, Boufounos, and Baraniuk [IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory (2013)] and has remained unresolved for over a decade, with subsequent sharp analyses studying a normalized variant instead, that additionally projects every iterate onto the unit sphere. This paper resolves that gap and characterizes when per-iterate normalization is algorithmically necessary. In the noiseless setting, we prove a universal, sample-optimal convergence theorem for the original BIHT algorithm. Specifically, with $\widetilde O(s/ε)$ measurements, a deterministic, computable finite-time iterate has directional error at most $ε$, simultaneously for every $s$-sparse unit vector. This matches the optimal sample dependence achieved by normalized BIHT in prior work. Under sign corruptions, we prove a sharp separation. If at most a $τ$ fraction of signs are flipped adversarially, then BIHT, without per-iterate normalization, still reaches the robust error floor at an early iterate with a matching $\widetilde O(s/ε)$ sample complexity rate as its normalized variant. This recovery, however, is not stable. We prove a scalar lower bound showing that any nontrivial corruption pattern, even one that involves only one flipped sign together with one clean sign, forces the iterates to oscillate indefinitely. Consequently, no general last-iterate convergence theorem can hold for BIHT under sign corruptions, while its normalized surrogate provably escapes this instance.

papers.title: Right $q$-Radial Calculus at Integral Superdimension
papers.abstract: We study the intrinsic right $q$-radial derivative at integral superdimension $M=m-2n$, using an independent formal parameter $Q$ before the specialisation $Q=q^M$. The exterior-blade action carries the parity factor $(-1)^{|I|}$, and the corresponding Fischer theory uses right multiplication. We establish finite-support compatibility, faithful coordinate realisations in a sufficient finite-block range, and localised Green and determinant-localised Fischer decompositions. For one vector, we determine the kernel and cokernel explicitly, including the additional singular monomial and missing image exactly when $M\in-2\mathbb N_0$. In degree zero the right Fischer operator is diagonal on auxiliary exterior blades, with eigenvalue $[M-p]_q+p$ at nonempty support rank $p$. For positive integral $M$, resonances in $0<q<1$ occur exactly at ranks $p>M$: each rank has one simple resonance, these values increase strictly with $p$, and the corresponding kernels and singular right-monogenic elements are explicit. The two-vector Fischer determinant is nonzero for positive $M$ and $0<q<1$.

papers.title: The exact region determined by Blomqvist's beta, Spearman's footrule and Kendall's tau
papers.abstract: We determine the exact region $Ω_{β,φ,τ}= \{(β(C),φ(C),τ(C))\mid C\in\mathcal{C}\}$ of possible joint values of Blomqvist's beta, Spearman's footrule and Kendall's tau over the class $\mathcal{C}$ of all bivariate copulas. The region consists precisely of all triples $(β,φ,τ)$ satisfying $-1\le β\le 1$, $\frac{3}{16}(1+β)^2-\frac12\le φ\le 1-\frac38(1-β)^2$ and $\frac43 φ-\frac13\le τ\le \frac23 φ+\frac13$. In other words, the known exact $(β,φ)$- and $(φ,τ)$-regions already characterize the joint region, so that, once the value of Spearman's footrule is fixed, Blomqvist's beta imposes no additional restriction on the possible values of Kendall's tau. The proof is constructive: two $2$-parameter families of shuffles of $M$ realize all the points in $Ω_{β,φ,τ}$ with $φ= \frac{3}{16}(1+β)^2-\frac12$, and ordinal sums spread realizations of these two families over the whole region $Ω_{β,φ,τ}$.

papers.title: Real and complex stability radii for a class of transport networks
papers.abstract: We characterize stability and its robustness for a class of boundary controlled, boundary observed hyperbolic partial differential equations. In particular, we show that asymptotic and exponential stability coincide for this class. Furthermore, we introduce the real and complex stability radii for which we give explicit formulas. In addition, we consider the dual system and its application to controllability and observability. Our main results are illustrated with two examples.

papers.title: The point-cross dimension
papers.abstract: Two transverse segments have local Hausdorff and upper box dimension one at their crossing, although they carry two independent tangent directions. We define the Point-Cross Dimension by assigning each tangent line the largest local upper box dimension captured by intersection with a regular \(C^1\) curve in that direction, then taking the supremum of their sums over finite independent families of tangent lines. Every Bouligand direction admits such a recurrent curve. The resulting profile is invariant under closure and covariant under local \(C^1\)-diffeomorphisms. Each directional weight is attained, and the profile is upper semicontinuous. An integral representation by ranks of weight superlevel sets gives submodularity and, together with projection bounds, exact Cartesian-product additivity. Germs with the same projective tangent support, local upper box dimension, and rank of segment directions can have different Point-Cross Dimensions. Further computations give exact directional profiles for chirps and the Point-Cross Dimension of a self-affine carpet. Finally, approximation of a ray with error \(O(t^d)\), for \(d>1\), forces directional weight at least \(1-1/d\), and this bound is sharp.

papers.title: Chromatic Constraints on Quantum Observables: Gaps, Contextuality, and Separability
papers.abstract: Intertwined complete projective experiments share outcomes, motivating the search for a common spectral labeling across contexts. Strong coloring tests whether complete contexts admit one context-independent nondegenerate spectrum; when that labeling exists, chromatic separability tests which event distinctions it preserves. We distinguish these questions from ordinary Kochen--Specker statelessness, geometric realizability, event-order representation, and Born-probability models. A state extends to a strong d-coloring exactly when deletion of its support leaves a (d-1)-colorable graph. Faithful real 17- and 21-ray restrictions of completed Yu--Oh have separating ordinary states but forced color identities; one quantum preparation requires exactly 1/9 nonextendable weight despite admitting an ordinary-state model. Independent Hermitian projection arguments correct earlier inferences from a chromatic gap to statelessness or nonrealizability. Hesse's complex 37-ray example separates real and complex geometry and has exact state-family minima 6/7/18 for three representation requirements. A rational two-plane construction gives a linear real 65-ray example with 393,216 states and explicit event-order and probability failures. General and specified ancestry results distinguish geometric KS extensions from abstract chromatic-to-stateless constructions. Detailed enumerations, regenerated state certificates, and extended proofs are supplementary.

papers.title: Rank-Two Drinfeld Modules over Elliptic Coordinate Rings
papers.abstract: Let ${\mathbf A}$ be the affine coordinate ring of $E\setminus\{\infty\}$, where $E$ is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb F_q$ and $\infty$ is rational. We solve the rank-two case of the open problem of explicitly classifying sign-normalized Drinfeld ${\mathbf A}$-modules in generic characteristic with a fixed determinant motive; the classification for rank greater than two remains open. Outside an explicit exceptional locus, the rank-two Drinfeld modules are parametrized by the open modular curve $Y^{q+1}=π(X)$ with $Y\neq0$. The polynomial $π$ is squarefree, and the smooth projective completion of this curve has genus $q^2$. The roots of $π$ split into two types. Above roots of the first type, all coefficient functions extend regularly, and their extensions yield exactly the exceptional modules. Roots of the second type correspond to cusps of the modular curve; above these roots, the coefficient family has poles.

papers.title: Singular stationary Navier-Stokes flows: examples and stability
papers.abstract: Landau solutions, when oriented along the vertical axis, represent a one parameter family of exact, self-similar, axisymmetric, swirl-free solutions to the 3D stationary Navier-Stokes equations forced by an upward facing point-source of momentum at the origin. They have an isolated singularity at the origin. Other singular steady state solutions can be derived from a similar framework. Some of these variants have been proposed as models for physical scenarios. For example, a solution first found by Squire has been proposed as a model of a fluid entrained to a radially discharging surface layer of oil. Another, Serrin's swirling vortex, exhibits qualitative features shared with some tornadoes, like a two-cell structure consisting of a central downdraft and peripheral updraft as well as swirl. The first objective of this paper is to provide a detailed analysis of these and other examples, especially when boundaries are present. In this direction we find several new, physically motivated classes of solutions and identify new connections between the physics literature and the mathematics literature. Many of these examples are formulated on the half-space, but much of the mathematical literature on singular steady-state solutions is for $\mathbb{R}^3$. The second objective of this paper is to establish asymptotic stability for many of these solutions by formulating the problem in domains with boundaries. Our most general result in this direction uses a new approach to asymptotic stability that is based on eventual regularity. In a different direction, we prove that a class of singular steady-state solutions motivated by Serrin's swirling vortex are stable under certain axisymmetric perturbations. This requires a novel observation because these ``Type III'' solutions are too singular to be directly amenable to existing approaches.

papers.title: Dual Gauss--Legendre polynomials
papers.abstract: We define and investigate two families of dual polynomials associated with the Gauss--Legendre polynomials, which have recently found interesting applications in computer graphics. Using the presented results, one can derive representations of the Gauss--Legendre polynomials, construct the dual bases for Lagrange bases and solve certain approximation problems arising, for example, in CAGD.

papers.title: Domination in Johnson graphs J(n, 3) for odd n
papers.abstract: In 2025 Cornet, Dravec, and Torres determined the domination number $γ(J(n,3))$ of the Johnson graph for every even $n \ge 6$, expressing it as a closed form $φ_n$ in terms of Fort-Hedlund covering numbers, and conjectured the same value for odd $n$. We prove this conjecture: $γ(J(n,3)) = φ_n$ for every odd $n \ge 7$. A dominating set of $J(n,3)$ is the same as a lotto design $\mathrm{LD}(n,3,3,2)$, and the lotto numbers $L(n,3,3,2)$, and hence $γ(J(n,3))$, were already determined for every $n$ by Bate (1978) and by Brouwer (1981). The contribution of this paper is therefore a new proof of the odd case, carried out within the bijective framework of Cornet, Dravec, and Torres.

papers.title: Branch and Price for Railway Crew Scheduling: Benchmark Instances and Computational Study
papers.abstract: Railway crew scheduling consists of assigning a set of tasks to crew members in the form of feasible duties so as to minimise costs, and is one of the key planning problems faced by railway operators. While column generation is the dominant solution method, literature on exact branch-and-price approaches is scarce. Moreover, few publicly available benchmark instances exist. We conduct a systematic computational study of branch and price for railway crew scheduling, evaluating the contribution of branching rules, primal heuristics, and reduced cost fixing. To this end, we introduce a novel library of 100 benchmark instances, ranging in size from 90 to 3,016 tasks, each provided in a single-depot and a multi-depot variant. The instances are generated by mimicking the railway planning process, validated against data from Netherlands Railways, and publicly available with best known solutions and a solution checker. We report average optimality gaps below 1% across all instance sizes, driven primarily by the strong performance of primal heuristics, whereas branching and reduced cost fixing contribute little to closing the gap. Branch and price also outperforms a multi-commodity flow formulation, which fails to find a feasible solution on many of the smallest instances. Our findings provide support for the popularity of column generation-based primal heuristics, and show that improving the dual bound remains the main challenge for exact methods in railway crew scheduling.

papers.title: A novel class of high-order uniformly accurate exponential integrators with local linear extension for the charged-particle dynamics under strong magnetic field
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel class of high-order uniformly accurate exponential integrators for charged-particle dynamics under strong magnetic field. The small parameter $0<\varepsilon\ll 1$ induces rapid temporal oscillations, rendering traditional numerical methods prohibitively expensive due to severe step-size restrictions. To address this issue, a linearization technology that introduces auxiliary polynomial variables is employed to recast the original charged-particle dynamics as a higher-dimensional system. Classical exponential integrators are subsequently applied to this augmented formulation, which inherently carries richer structural information, thereby yielding a family of uniformly accurate exponential integrators that can reach arbitrarily high order without requiring any order conditions. For strong magnetic fields under the maximal-ordering scaling, we rigorously establish through algebraic techniques that the schemes with auxiliary polynomial variables of degree $k\geq2$ achieve an improved position error bound of $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k+1}h,\varepsilon h^{k+1}\})$ and a uniform velocity error bound of $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k}h,h^{k+1}\})$, where $h$ denotes the time-step size. Under the additional condition that the magnetic field gradient vanishes at the origin, these bounds sharpen to $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k+2},\varepsilon h^{k+1}\})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k+1},h^{k+1}\})$ for the position and velocity, respectively, for $k\geq1$. The same sharper bounds hold for constant strong magnetic fields. Numerical experiments confirm the advantages of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Amplituhedra and origami, II: loop level
papers.abstract: Building on the recently discovered origami-amplituhedron correspondence, we prove that the BCFW (Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten) cells triangulate the $m=4$ amplituhedron in full generality at all loop orders, both in momentum and momentum-twistor space. Along the way, we develop two natural "$L$-punctured" extensions of the positive Grassmannian and relate them via T-duality.

papers.title: Long Time Well-posedness for the Benjamin-Ono Equation with Quasi-Periodic Initial Data
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the long time well-posedness of the Benjamin-Ono (BO) equation with quasi-periodic initial data in analytic space. We demonstrate that the Lax operator of the BO equation exhibits a trivial spectrum, and elucidate the fundamental mathematical obstacles to establishing global well-posedness. Furthermore, by employing Tao's gauge transformation in conjunction with the Birkhoff Normal Form method, we extend the lifespan of the solutions to $O(ε^{-3})$.

papers.title: Mixed-Precision GPU Acceleration for Large-Scale Minimum Enclosing Ball Problems
papers.abstract: A mixed-precision GPU-oriented optimization framework is developed for computing the minimum enclosing ball of a collection of balls. The approach is built on an equivalent second-order cone programming reformulation and a relative-type inexact proximal augmented Lagrangian method (ripALM), which provides a high-accuracy optimization backbone while solving the inner subproblems only to a progress-dependent relative accuracy. The proximal augmented Lagrangian inherits a constraint-wise separable structure: its objective, gradient, generalized Hessian, and multiplier updates can be efficiently evaluated on GPUs as parallel maps over the input balls followed by reductions. To further improve efficiency, a mixed-precision reduction strategy is introduced. A low-precision ripALM run identifies balls near the approximate boundary, a high-precision ripALM run refines the reduced problem, and a full a posteriori feasibility check detects and reintroduces any violated discarded balls. Thus, low precision is used only for screening and warm starting, while the final feasibility is enforced against the original problem. Experiments on synthetic and real-data instances show that the proposed methods can compute accurate solutions, with GPU execution providing substantial speedups and mixed-precision reduction further reducing running times on most tested instances.

papers.title: Reachability-Augmented Dual Dynamic Programming for Optimal Path Parameterization
papers.abstract: Optimal path parameterization (OPP) is a fundamental problem for planning trajectories along a prescribed geometric path under kinodynamic constraints and task-dependent objectives. Among existing OPP works, it remains challenging to simultaneously achieve feasibility guarantees, general-objective optimality certificates, and online-compatible computation in a unified framework, especially for third-order OPP (OPP3) with non-convex constraints. This paper proposes reachability-augmented dual dynamic programming (RDDP), a state-grid-free and objective-aware dynamic programming (DP) framework for OPP. The key idea is to replace the relatively complete recourse assumption used in classical dual DP (DDP) with OPP-specific backward reachable sets, and then generate both value-function cuts and trial trajectories only inside these reachable sets. For convex and non-convex OPP, we prove global optimality and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker convergence of RDDP under OPP-specific conditions, respectively. Efficient instantiations are developed for second-order OPP (OPP2) and OPP3. Experiments show that RDDP achieves objective values comparable to convex-optimization baselines with speedups of approximately 15.3 and 4.9 times over the fastest of 4 tested solvers for OPP2 and OPP3, respectively. RDDP also achieves faster convergence than grid-based DP. Compared with reachability-analysis methods, RDDP retains the reachability mechanism while replacing local maximum-control propagation with value-function-guided control selection, thereby enabling objectives beyond traversal time. In summary, RDDP addresses a key capability gap in OPP by unifying certifiable general-objective optimization, reachability-based feasibility preservation, and online-compatible low-dimensional DP computation in a single framework.

papers.title: One Model, Two Roles: Emergent Specialization in a Shared Recurrent Transformer
papers.abstract: Can a shared-weight recurrent Transformer---one that repeatedly applies the same Transformer to update evolving latent states---develop distinct internal roles without being partitioned into separate modules? We study this in Asymmetric Input Recurrence (AIR), a minimal two-state reasoning architecture in which the same Transformer model is reused for both updates (per literature, L and H) and the only built-in difference in the update rule is that the encoded input is injected during L-updates but not H-updates. Across Sudoku-Extreme and Maze, decoded rollouts reveal a consistent split: $z_H$ behaves like a fully committed proposal state, whereas $z_L$ retains local uncertainty and shifting intermediate structure. Freeze interventions provide evidence of dynamical dependence between the two states, with responses that vary across tasks, intervention directions, and seeds. Ablations show that to induce specialization, the shared model needs to be able to tell the two update types apart, either from input injection asymmetry or from a separate level token. Mechanistically, attention analysis shows that L-updates are consistently more local than H-updates in both Sudoku and Maze. Together, these results show that, in a two-state recurrent setting, a clear state-identity signal can induce stable, related functional roles inside a shared-parameter recurrent Transformer. Code is available at https://github.com/juchengshen/air.

papers.title: Approximate Dynamic Programming for Real-time Assignment of Extraboard Transit Operators
papers.abstract: This study investigates real-time assignment decisions for extraboard transit operators, who are responsible for covering open work due to unexpected events such as driver absenteeism. Efficient usage of extraboard operators is critical as open work negatively affects service reliability. The problem is formulated as a Markov decision process, designed to capture its stochastic and sequential nature. Due to the problem's very large state space, an approximate policy is proposed in the form of an integer program, which maps a system state to assignment decisions such that the sum of immediate and expected future rewards is maximized. As part of off-line training, future value functions for individual operators are computed using a backward dynamic program. Then, the overestimation in the aggregate value obtained by summing individual values is corrected to account for the interaction among operators. Case studies are conducted based on the operations at a real-world transit agency. Key performance metrics including uncovered open work and extraboard utilization rates are examined for varying absenteeism rates and extraboard roster sizes. The approximate policy is shown to outperform benchmark decision rules mirroring real-world assignment strategies. Further numerical experiments are conducted to analyze different operational policies: (1) inclusion of overtime drivers in the reserve operator roster; (2) reward weights for work tasks that consider passenger wait time saved. Observations from these computational analyses provide actionable insights into extraboard sizing, overtime usage, and real-time dispatch practices at transit agencies.

papers.title: A Provably Convergent and Practical Algorithm for Gromov--Wasserstein Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Gromov--Wasserstein optimal transport (GWOT) aligns metric measure spaces by matching their within-domain relational structures, but large-scale GWOT remains challenging because its objective is nonconvex and projection onto the transport polytope is often solved only approximately in practice. This leads to a gap between practical projected-gradient implementations and convergence theory, which typically assumes exact projections. For squared-loss GWOT, we propose an inexact projected-gradient framework with a verifiable feasibility-residual-based inexact condition for the projection subproblem. This condition is directly computable and avoids unknown quantities such as the exact projection point. Under this implementable condition, we prove subsequential convergence to stationary points and, with a mild tolerance-decay condition, convergence of the whole sequence. The resulting method retains the simplicity and sparsity of projected-gradient schemes while providing rigorous convergence guarantees, turning projected-gradient methods into a principled and scalable approach for GWOT with provable reliability.

papers.title: A neural network method for scalar conservation laws with convergence rates for shock waves
papers.abstract: We propose a new entropy-compatible neural network method for scalar hyperbolic conservation laws and establish, to our knowledge, the first explicit $L^1$ convergence rates in this setting for piecewise smooth entropy solutions, including those with discontinuities. The method is based on a computable approximation of the Kružkov entropy residual that sits between the strong and weak forms of the entropy inequality. For a single regular shock in one dimension and finitely many smooth shock hypersurfaces with transversal interactions in several dimensions, we construct explicit neural networks with provably small loss by combining shock-adapted continuous piecewise linear functions with known approximation properties of $\tanh$ neural networks. The one-dimensional analysis also covers rarefactions, compound waves, regular shock interactions, and nondegenerate shock formation from smooth initial data. Together with entropy-based stability estimates, this gives rigorous $L^1$ error bounds for minimizers of the proposed loss. In particular, when the network size grows in proportion to the number of degrees of freedom of a space--time mesh of size $h$, the analysis recovers the classical Kuznetsov rate $O(h^{1/2})$ in shock-dominated cases. Numerical experiments in one and two space dimensions illustrate the performance of the method.

papers.title: The $\mathbf{P}^1$-motivic Gysin map
papers.abstract: We develop a $\mathbf{P}^1$-unstable non-$\mathbf{A}^1$-invariant theory of motivic spaces and spectra, and construct the Gysin map therein for regular immersions. This in particular gives the Gysin map in the Annala--Hoyois--Iwasa $\mathbf{P}^1$-motivic spectra, and thus gives a uniform construction for the Gysin maps of various cohomology theories.

papers.title: A PDE formulation of Lyapunov stability for contact-type Hamilton-Jacobi equations
papers.abstract: We study the Lyapunov stability of stationary viscosity solutions of contact-type Hamilton--Jacobi equations on a compact manifold. We consider Hamiltonians of the form $H(x,p,u)=G(x,p)+W(x,u)$, where $G$ is continuous, convex and coercive in $p$. We establish sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability and instability in terms of viscosity subsolutions and one-sided derivatives of a perturbed critical value. These criteria do not require the construction of a smooth contact Hamiltonian flow. Under the stability condition, solutions starting sufficiently close to a stationary solution converge to it at an exponential rate. To prove instability, we use the superposition principle for closed measures to construct calibrated curves. We also establish conditions ensuring uniqueness of stationary solutions and global asymptotic stability. Our results also cover examples with nonmonotone dependence on the unknown function, including an equation with an eikonal term $|p|$. Finally, we obtain an $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ convergence rate for a class of stationary Hamilton--Jacobi equations with nonlinear dependence on the unknown function and multiscale spatial dependence.

papers.title: Evaluation of Gauss-Legendre curves
papers.abstract: We present new representations of Gauss--Legendre polynomials and their derivatives in the shifted power basis and in bases related to symmetric orthogonal Jacobi polynomials. Using these representations and certain recurrence relations, we propose $O(n^2+dn)$ methods for evaluating a Gauss--Legendre curve of degree $n$ in $\mathbb E^d$. We also propose algorithms for multipoint evaluation with computational complexity $O(Mdn+dn^2)$, where $M$ is the number of evaluation points. Numerical tests show that the approach using the shifted power basis is very fast, but it works well only for small $n$ (approximately up to 20), whereas the method employing Jacobi polynomials gives good numerical results even for large $n$ (around 100).

papers.title: The cohesive and stable Ramsey theorems and proof size over a weak base theory
papers.abstract: We show that over the weak base theory $\mathrm{RCA}_0^*$, cohesive Ramsey's theorem for pairs $\mathrm{CRT}^2_2$ implies exponential closure of the definable cut $\mathrm{I}^0_1$, which is the intersection of all $Σ^0_1$-definable cuts. Consequences include non-elementary proof speedup of $\mathrm{RCA}_0^* + \mathrm{CRT}^2_2$ over $\mathrm{RCA}_0^*$ for $Π_1$ sentences and the unprovability of $\mathrm{CRT}^2_2$ in $\mathrm{RCA}_0^* + \mathrm{CAC}$. On the other hand, we show that $\mathrm{RCA}_0^* + \mathrm{SRT}^2_2$, where $\mathrm{SRT}^2_2$ is stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs, is polynomially simulated by $\mathrm{RCA}_0^*$ with respect to proofs of $\forall Π^0_3$ sentences. Nevertheless, $\mathrm{SRT}^2_2$ also implies a nontrivial property of $\mathrm{I}^0_1$, specifically closure under functions of quasipolynomial growth rate.

papers.title: The Bernstein-von Mises theorem and efficiency for semiparametric inference in multivariate Hawkes processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study semiparametric inference for linear multivariate Hawkes processes, a class of point processes widely used to describe self and mutually exciting phenomena. We establish a convolution theorem giving the best limiting distribution for a regular estimator of smooth functional. Then, in the Bayesian setting, we prove a semiparametric Bernstein-von Mises (BvM) theorem for nonparametric random series priors. We apply this result to histogram and wavelet based priors. Taken together, the convolution and BvM theorems show that, from a frequentist point of view, semiparametric Bayesian procedures have asymptotically the optimal behavior. Deriving the BvM property for random series priors led us to prove L2 posterior contraction, complementing for these priors the results of Donnet, Rivoirard and Rousseau (2020).

papers.title: Activate the Dual Cones: A Tight Reformulation of Conic ACOPF Constraints
papers.abstract: By exploiting the observed tightness of dual rotated second-order cone (RSOC) constraints, this paper transforms the dual of a conic ACOPF relaxation into an equivalent, non-conic problem where dual constraints are implicitly enforced through eliminated dual RSOC variables. To accomplish this, we apply the RSOC-based Jabr relaxation of ACOPF, pose its dual, and then show that all dual RSOC constraints must be tight (i.e., active) at optimality. We then construct a reduced dual maximization problem with only non-negativity constraints, avoiding the explicit RSOC inequality constraints. Numerical experiments confirm that the tight formulation recovers the same dual objective values as a mature conic solver (e.g., MOSEK via PowerModels) on various PGLib benchmark test systems (ranging from 3- to 1354-buses). The proposed formulation has useful performance benefits, compared with its conic counterpart, and it allows us to define a bounding function which provides a guaranteed lower bound on system cost. While this paper focuses on demonstrating the correctness and validity of the proposed structural simplification, it lays the groundwork for future GPU-accelerated first-order optimization methods which can exploit the unconstrained nature of the proposed formulation.

papers.title: A Spectral Perspective on Stochastic Control Barrier Functions
papers.abstract: Stochastic control barrier functions (SCBFs) provide a safety-critical control framework for systems subject to stochastic disturbances by bounding the probability of remaining within a safe set. However, finding a valid SCBF that explicitly reflects the long-horizon behavior of the true safety probability remains a challenge. This paper addresses this issue by adopting a spectral perspective, utilizing the linear operator that governs the evolution of the closed-loop system's safety probability. We find that the dominant eigenpair of this Koopman-like operator encodes fundamental safety information of the stochastic system. The dominant eigenfunction is a natural and valid SCBF, with values that characterize relative asymptotic safety across initial states, while the dominant eigenvalue indicates the global asymptotic rate at which the safety probability decays. A practical algorithm for computation is proposed, termed power-policy iteration, which jointly estimates the dominant eigenpair while updating the backup policy with the aim of improving long-term safety. The method is validated using simulation experiments on safety-critical dynamics models.

papers.title: On $w$-Hilbert domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of a $w$-Hilbert domain and investigate its basic properties. More precisely, we explore its relationship with Hilbert domains, strong Mori domains, and UMT domains by providing various examples using $D+M$ constructions. Furthermore, we characterize the polynomial rings and some of their extensions that are $w$-Hilbert domains.

papers.title: Towards the characterization of minimum weight codewords of Schubert codes
papers.abstract: A formula for the minimum weight of Schubert codes was conjectured by Ghorpade and Lachaud in 2000. This was established by Xiang in 2008. In 2018, Ghorpade and Singh provided a new proof of this conjecture. Moreover, they also conjectured that the minimum weight codewords of the Schubert codes $C_\a (\ell, m)$ are given by the so-called \emph{Schubert decomposable codewords}. We prove the validity of the conjecture for all Schubert varieties $Ω_{\a}(\ell, V_m)$ for all but finitely many values of $q$.

papers.title: Dimension-Independent Convergence of Underdamped Langevin Monte Carlo in KL Divergence
papers.abstract: Underdamped Langevin dynamics (ULD) is a widely-used sampler for Gibbs distributions $π\propto e^{-V}$, and is often empirically effective in high dimensions.
