papers.title: Kernel representations of fractional gradient bilinear forms. Part II. Variable coefficients
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the existence and properties of interaction kernels representing nonlocal energies associated with the Riesz fractional gradient and variable, uniformly elliptic matrix fields $A(x)$. Building on our previous analysis of constant matrices in [DSV26], we establish necessary conditions on the singularity and decay of such kernels, derive an explicit representation formula under suitable regularity assumptions, and prove uniqueness of the kernel representation. We also obtain sharp asymptotics and positivity criteria near the diagonal, averaged decay estimates at infinity, and characterize the divergence free property of $A(x)$ through the decay of the kernel. Finally, we show that the associated energy may fail the truncation property and that arbitrarily small smooth perturbations of constant matrices can destroy the nonnegativity of the representing kernel. These results provide negative answers to both [SS18, Open Problems 1.9 and 1.10].

papers.title: Inexact PDHG for Large-Scale Semidefinite Programming
papers.abstract: First-order methods, such as the primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method, have recently been explored for large-scale semidefinite programming (SDP). However, exact projections can be computationally prohibitive, motivating inexact projections using conditional gradient methods. Although computationally cheap and projection-free, these methods typically converge sublinearly. Recent variants, such as Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe (Garber, 2026), achieve linear convergence in expectation near the optimal face of the spectrahedron. We develop an inexact PDHG framework with tractable spectrahedral projections using two techniques: (i) adaptive error tolerances that avoid unnecessary inner iterations while guaranteeing convergence, and (ii) a heuristic spectral warm start based on the Lanczos algorithm that accelerates Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe by initializing near the optimal face. We establish an O(1/t) convergence rate for PDHG in the presence of projection errors and estimate the total number of inner iterations required for convergence. Experiments on large-scale SDP instances demonstrate that combining spectral warm starts with Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe outperforms Lanczos-based inexact projections.

papers.title: Calabi-Yau Hyperbolicity
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to introduce a new notion of hyperbolicity for compact complex manifolds with trivial canonical bundle, called \textit{Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity}. We investigate its fundamental properties and establish a characterization in terms of the fundamental group. In particular, we show that no compact Kähler Calabi--Yau manifold is Calabi--Yau hyperbolic, highlighting the genuinely non-Kähler nature of this notion. We also investigate different techniques for constructing examples of such manifolds. Finally, we examine the relationship between Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity and Kobayashi hyperbolicity in the examples considered, highlighting obstructions to the latter in the Calabi--Yau setting.

papers.title: Diffraction of rotated measures
papers.abstract: Consider a translation-bounded measure on the line. We can rotate the measure, distributing the mass proportionally to the area, to create a two-dimensional rotationally invariant translation-bounded measure. We show that the diffraction of the two-dimensional object is the normalised rotation of the diffraction of the original measure. We discuss some examples and generalisation beyond $d=2$.

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved periods in a cyclic-dominance automaton: separating intrinsic from lattice-induced periodicity
papers.abstract: Periodic attractors of spatially extended systems possess not one period but a hierarchy of periods, one for each level of observation and symmetry quotient, and this hierarchy separates how a pattern evolves from how it fits the finite domain. For a synchronous threshold model of cyclic dominance on an $L\times L$ torus, equivalent to the three-color cyclic cellular automaton of Fisch, Gravner and Griffeath, we measure for every attractor a \emph{tuple} of periods: that of the populations ($\Tpop$), of the full configuration ($\Tst$), and of the configuration up to color rotations ($\Tcol$), lattice symmetries ($\Tgeo$) and the full space--color group ($\TG$). Equivariance implies exact divisibility relations and the factorization $\Tst=\TG\,m$, where $m$ counts the applications of the symmetry $h$ that maps the configuration onto itself after $\TG$ steps: $\TG$ and the type of $h$ belong to the pattern, $m$ to the lattice, and the attractors are relative periodic orbits whose full period emerges from the interaction between the intrinsic dynamics and the lattice symmetries. A family of attractors built around a pair of counter-rotating spirals, with $\Tpop=24$ and $\TG=8$, persists from $L=9$ to $L=40$ while $\Tst$ takes values from 24 to 960, given in every case by the order of $h$; on a rectangular $9\times12$ torus it takes the value 48, absent from all square tori. With more than $4.5\times10^5$ runs at each of $L=8$ and $L=9$ we estimate the basins of attraction: fixed points take 95--97\% of the configuration space, and no single period is enough to tell the oscillating attractors apart. The same analysis locates local diversity: it is balanced whenever the cycle has a color symmetry and, on large lattices, it is concentrated at the spiral cores.

papers.title: Fisher Geometry of Circular Wrapped Normals: Completion and Curvature
papers.abstract: We determine the intrinsic Fisher geometry of the two-parameter circular wrapped normal family. Although its finite parameters form a cylinder, its metric completion is a disk: adjoining the uniform law extends the Fisher metric to a positive-definite real-analytic metric. The Gaussian curvature vanishes at the added point, is positive nearby, and tends to $-1/2$ as the underlying standard deviation tends to zero. We prove that the curvature has exactly one nonuniform zero radius and exactly one critical radius, the latter a nondegenerate positive maximum. Opposite points sufficiently close to uniformity are joined by a unique minimizing geodesic through the uniform law, so their intrinsic distance is not attained inside the nonuniform family. In contrast, identifying the means of real normal distributions modulo a period retains a complete hyperbolic cylinder with an infinitely distant cusp. Wrapping strictly decreases Fisher information in every nonzero tangent direction, while the information deficit and its fixed-order derivatives are exponentially small as the standard deviation tends to zero. The curvature theorem is proved by convergent series and explicit analytic remainder estimates; numerical figures serve only as illustrations.

papers.title: Spectral unions of four intervals tile the real line
papers.abstract: We prove that every spectral union of four bounded intervals tiles the real line by translations. The argument combines periodicity of spectra, cofactor identities for the secular determinant, and a common tiling complement for the finite spectral fibers. We also establish a rigidity theorem for six complex numbers with prescribed vanishing power sums.

papers.title: Diagrams for Roots and Quiver Representations in the context of the Gabriel-Kac Theorem
papers.abstract: Using the data of the Dynkin diagrams, we build graphical calculi for representing the positive roots of Kac-Moody algebras and the representations of quivers. Once developed, we use these to analyze the asymptotic size of the root and representation spaces, and discuss how this relates to the Gabriel-Kac theorem, the correspondence between these two structures. We give a refinement of this correspondence in terms of the trichotomy of growth rates for Kac-Moody algebras depending on if they are of finite, affine, or indefinite type, which is done in terms of what we call ``tree like" representations.

papers.title: On the cohomological dimension of Henselian valued fields
papers.abstract: Let $(K,v)$ be a Henselian valued field of rank one and of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, with value group $Γ$ dense in $\mathbb{R}$ and residue field $k$. We compute all the graded pieces of the filtration induced by $v$ on the Milnor $\mathrm{K}$-theory modulo $p$ of $K$, in terms of the exterior powers of the $\mathbb{F}_p$-vector space $Γ/pΓ$ and of the modules of differential forms of $k$. This extends to the non-discrete setting a classical theorem of Kato concerning complete discretely valued fields. We also prove that, when $(K,v)$ is maximally complete, no class escapes this filtration by accumulating at a limit. As an application, we prove the inequality $\dim_p(K)\geq\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}(Γ/pΓ)+\dim_p(k)$ between Kato's $p$-dimensions, and we show that it becomes an equality as soon as $(K,v)$ is maximally complete.

papers.title: Torsion Theories in a non-pointed Context II: iterated torsion theories
papers.abstract: Generalizing a known result in the context of homological categories, we show that, in a regular protomodular category $\mathcal{C}$ equipped with a posetal, monocoreflective subcategory whose coreflector inverts monomorphisms, every torsion theory, in a non-pointed sense, satisfying suitable properties gives rise to a torsion theory in the category $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ of arrows in $\mathcal{C}$. Moreover, we show that the induced torsion theory in $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ satisfies the same good properties of the original one in $\mathcal{C}$, allowing to iterate the process. Examples of this situation can be found in protomodular varieties of universal algebras with more than one constant or in duals of elementary toposes.

papers.title: SAG-Sep: Sparse Augmented Graphs and Onion-Guided Search for Rounded Capacity Cut Separation
papers.abstract: Rounded capacity cuts (RCCs) are among the most effective cuts for capacitated vehicle-routing relaxations, but exact separation is computationally prohibitive at scale. Existing heuristic and neural separators can be fast, but often fail to produce sufficiently many effective cuts within practical separation budgets. We introduce SAG-Sep, a separator that scores node membership in RCC-inducing subsets across vehicle-count levels from a fractional LP solution in a single encoder forward pass, avoiding the iterative predict-and-coarsen inference used by NeuralSEP-style separators. SAG-Sep encodes the LP solution as a Sparse Augmented Graph (SAG), adding flow-informed multi-hop edges that expose long-range routing structure without densifying attention. Beyond LP-aware sparse encoding, we observe that high-value exact RCCs are typically nested, organizing into onion-like subset families, and SAG-Sep's node scores track subset nesting depth. This motivates Onion-Sweep (OS), a training-free decoder that ranks customers by their scores, evaluates the RCC violation of every prefix of the ranking in one vectorized pass, and emits the most violated prefix of each replica together with a cross-replica family of nested proposals, converting independent node scores into structurally coordinated RCC candidates without a tuned threshold or probing band. On the NeuralSEP benchmark with N=1000 customer instances, SAG-Sep with OS reduces the average root gap by 17.7% relative to the strongest NeuralSEP baseline, while the single-pass SAG-Sep separator achieves a roughly 30-fold per-iteration neural separation speedup. Our findings suggest that LP-aware sparse encoding and the nested structure of high-value cuts are structural patterns worth leveraging in neural separation more broadly.

papers.title: A Stochastic LineseArch Method (SLAM) for Minimizing Expectation Residuals: Weakening Boundedness of Gradient
papers.abstract: We establish convergence guarantees for the Stochastic LineseArch Method (SLAM) proposed and analyzed in Wang et al. (arXiv:2512.14979) for nonconvex composite stochastic optimization, retaining the iteration and sample complexity orders of the original analysis assuming neither the boundedness of true gradients nor the Lipschitz continuity of the convex nonsmooth term $r$. ChatGPT was used to assist in developing a key intermediate result. Under uniformly Lipschitz continuous and unbiased sampled gradients with uniformly bounded variance with mini-batch sizes proportional to the iteration budget, SLAM achieves an iteration complexity $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ and a sample complexity $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-4})$ for obtaining an iterate whose expected proximal-gradient residual norm is at most $ε$.

papers.title: Van der Waerden's Problem for Cubic Surfaces
papers.abstract: For a smooth cubic surface $S/\mathbb{Q}$, the absolute Galois group acts on the $27$ lines of $S_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$, giving a subgroup \[ G_S\subseteq W(E_6). \] We study the distribution of $G_S$ when the twenty coefficients of a defining cubic form are chosen independently from a large interval $[-H,H]$. We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, the number of smooth integral cubic forms of height at most $H$ for which \[ G_S\neq W(E_6) \] is \[ O_\varepsilon\!\left(H^{19+1/21+\varepsilon}\right). \] The principal obstruction is the unique subgroup $W(E_6)^+$ of index $2$. By a theorem of Saito, membership in this subgroup is equivalent to the signed discriminant of the cubic surface being a square. A recent square-value estimate of Bonolis, Pierce, and Woo then gives the exponent $19+1/21$. For each of the other five conjugacy classes of maximal subgroups of $W(E_6)$, recent results on rational points in projective thin sets give the sharper bound $O(H^{19})$. We also prove the lower bound \[ N_{\mathrm{exc}}(H)\gg H^{16} \] by counting cubic surfaces containing a fixed rational line, and exhibit an $H^{14}$-sized exceptional family with no rational line, arising from rational Eckardt points. These examples lead us to conjecture that \[ N_{\mathrm{exc}}(H)=H^{16+o(1)}. \] Finally, we investigate whether Bhargava's proof of van der Waerden's conjecture for $S_n$ can be adapted to the index-$2$ $E_6$-problem. A double-discriminant argument gives the desired $H^{19+\varepsilon}$ bound whenever the product of the strongly square-dividing primes is sufficiently large. The remaining difficulty comes from weak square divisibility.

papers.title: Symmetric List Objects
papers.abstract: Cons-lists are fundamental to functional programming, and are well-understood as initial algebras, and as a concrete construction of free monoids. In category theory, such list objects can be axiomatised internal to any monoidal category, with nil and cons maps, and a recursion mechanism. When strengthened to support parametrised recursion, they can be shown to give the free monoid construction. We study a small variant on parametrised list objects called parametrised symmetric list objects, in a symmetric monoidal category, where the two frontmost elements are allowed to be permuted. We show that this gives a construction of free commutative monoids, and develop some related theory.

papers.title: An Introduction to the Obstacle Problem
papers.abstract: We give a self-contained account of the classical obstacle problem, written for graduate students who wish to enter the field of free boundary problems. Starting from a one-dimensional model and an explicit radially symmetric example, we set up the variational problem, show that minimizers exist and are unique, and prove interior $W^{2,p}$-regularity as well as the optimal $C^{1,1}$-regularity. The second half of the notes is devoted to the free boundary: we prove that it is porous, introduce blow-up limits, and use the Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman monotonicity formula to show that every free boundary point is either regular or singular. These notes grew out of a mini-course at the Rio Summer School on PDEs in 2020, and they are meant to be read alongside, not instead of, the monograph by Petrosyan, Shahgholian, and Uraltseva.

papers.title: Enumeration Complexity of Permutation Classes
papers.abstract: We study classes of permutations that are defined by avoidance of forbidden patterns. For each fixed finite set $B$ of forbidden patterns, we study the \emph{avoider enumeration problem}: given an integer $n$, output all $B$-avoiding permutations of length $n$. Avoider enumeration is output-polynomial for every fixed $B$. However, our main notion of efficiency is polynomial delay. We use the insert-maximum tree as a search tree, in which permutations are built by repeatedly inserting a new maximum while preserving pattern avoidance. This leads to the \emph{insert-maximum extension problem}, which asks if a given permutation has an avoiding descendant at a specified depth. An algorithm for this problem can prune branches that cannot reach the target length. Hence, if this problem is in P, we obtain polynomial-delay enumeration. To investigate this problem, we introduce and study \emph{pockets}, the maximal finite subtrees of the insert-maximum tree. For fixed $B$, if there is a polynomial $p$ such that every pocket rooted at $ρ$ has at most $p(|ρ|)$ nodes, then the extension problem is solvable in polynomial time and enumeration has polynomial delay. In particular, a bound on pocket depth depending only on $B$ suffices. We prove such a bound if the class is well-quasi-ordered, has a regular insertion encoding, or if $B$ omits one of the three maximum-position types: leftmost, interior, or rightmost. We also prove that extension is in NP for every fixed $B$, even with binary-encoded target depth. On the negative side, we construct a fixed set of $55$ forbidden patterns for which extension is NP-complete. Consequently, enumerating valid extensions from a given starting permutation cannot have polynomial delay unless P=NP. This also answers a question of Hanika by showing that the forbidden permutation constraint satisfaction problem can be NP-complete for a fixed forbidden set.

papers.title: Generalised hyperbolic polynomials: combinatorial interpretation and real-rootedness
papers.abstract: For $p,q$ natural numbers, define $Δ^{\langle p,q \rangle}:=x^{p-1}\frac{\partial}{\partial y} + y^{q-1}\frac{\partial}{\partial x}$, and consider the sequence of polynomials $\biggl((Δ^{\langle p,q \rangle})^n \cdot x\biggr)_{n\geq 0}$; we call these the generalised hyperbolic polynomials. In this paper, we provide a simple combinatorial interpretation for these polynomials. As special cases, we obtain combinatorial interpretations for the coefficients of the analogs of sinh and cosh corresponding to the curve $x^p- p y^q/q=1$; on setting $p=q=3$, we obtain Conrad and Flajolet's tree interpretation for the coefficients of the Dixonian elliptic functions (2006) as a special case. Finally, we show that for any $p,q\geq 3$, after suitably normalising followed by substituting $y=1$, we obtain a sequence of univariate polynomials which are real-rooted.

papers.title: On End-Semidualizing Modules
papers.abstract: We introduce and study the notion of End-semidualizing modules which are generalizations of semidualizing modules in the classical sense, and also extend the notion of $S-R$ semidualizing bimodules studied by Holm-White and Wakamatsu. By constrast with these notions, End-semidualizing modules exist abundantly. We characterize these modules by the inclusion of projective and flat modules in their Auslander class, or injective modules in their Bass class, and give criteria for when these Foxby classes satisfy the two-out-of-three property. Over commutative Noetherian rings, we prove base-change and duality results, and characterize local depth inequalities by the inclusion of all modules of finite flat or injective dimension in the corresponding classes.

papers.title: High-chromatic tournament parts without a complete pair of cyclic triangles
papers.abstract: Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour conjectured that any two disjoint subtournaments of sufficiently large chromatic number contain cyclic triangles, one in each subtournament, with all edges between them oriented in the same direction. We disprove this conjecture by constructing, for every positive integer $d$, a tournament $T$ with a vertex partition $(X,Y)$ such that $χ(T[X]),χ(T[Y])\ge d$, but no cyclic triangle in either part is complete to a cyclic triangle in the other. Our construction combines a graph of large girth and large chromatic number with a variant of Kneser graphs defined in terms of binary functions. We give two proofs of the required chromatic lower bound, one using the Borsuk--Ulam theorem and the other using the octahedral form of Tucker's lemma.

papers.title: Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals: Absorption Probabilities and Conic Intrinsic Volumes
papers.abstract: Let $(U_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process in $\mathbb R^d$ whose coordinate processes $(U_t^{(i)})_{t\in\mathbb R}$, $1\le i\le d$, are independent, centered, and have covariance function $\mathbb E [U_s^{(i)}U_t^{(i)}]=e^{-|t-s|/2}$. For every $T>0$, we obtain an explicit formula for the probability that the convex hull $\mathrm{conv}\{U_t:0\le t\le T\}$ contains the origin. We obtain a similar formula for a circular Ornstein--Uhlenbeck loop whose covariance is the normalized $T$-periodization of this kernel. For each fixed dimension $d$, we determine the precise long-time asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities, which decay as explicit constants times $T^{d-1} e^{-T/2}$ as $T\to\infty$. We also show that, as $d\to\infty$, the absorption probabilities in both models undergo a transition from $0$ to $1$ around $T=2d$, with a common Gaussian limiting profile on the scale $\sqrt d$. We also obtain explicit formulas for the probability that $σZ$ belongs to the convex hull of Brownian motion or Brownian bridge on $[0,1]$ in $\mathbb R^d$, where $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian vector and $σ\ge0$. The large-$σ$ asymptotics recover the known formulas for the expected volumes of these convex hulls. Finally, we compute the conic intrinsic volumes of the closed positive hulls of deterministic Ornstein--Uhlenbeck spirals and their circular analogues in Hilbert spaces. Their Grassmann angles coincide with the corresponding Ornstein--Uhlenbeck absorption probabilities. After suitable rescaling, the small-time limits of these conic intrinsic volumes recover the formulas of Gao--Vitale and Gao for the intrinsic volumes of the Brownian body and its Brownian-bridge analogue.

papers.title: Hierarchical Laminates Cannot Reproduce All Effective Properties of Planar Two-Phase Composites: A Counterexample with a 16-Component Potential
papers.abstract: Designing a composite requires understanding which effective properties can be achieved through varying its microstructure, i.e., the spatial arrangement of given constituent materials. Hierarchical laminates, created by successive layering, reach many known limits on these properties, making it natural to ask whether they can reproduce every effective response obtainable from the same constituents. We answer this question negatively for planar two-phase composites governed by linear systems whose potentials have 16 or more components. We construct constituent material properties and, at any prescribed nontrivial phase fraction, periodic microstructures whose effective properties cannot be approximated by hierarchical laminates, even when layer directions, proportions, and the number of layering steps are unrestricted. We design the constituents so that all hierarchical laminates have equal effective energies at two prescribed mean gradients. The key step is to construct a medium whose local properties are those of horizontal laminates with smoothly varying phase fractions, but whose effective energies violate this equality. Approximating these energies with sufficiently fine periodic stripes of the original constituents yields the two-phase counterexample. This construction also gives a negative answer to the two-well relaxation problem: the minimum of two positive-definite homogeneous quadratic forms on $\mathbb{R}^{2\times32}$ can have distinct quasiconvex and rank-one convex envelopes. The counterexample and the strict inequality between the envelopes are formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: Lie (super)algebras generated by reflections in finite reflection groups of exceptional type
papers.abstract: Using a mixture of theoretical tools and computer calculations, we describe the Lie subalgebras and the Lie sub-superalgebras generated by the sets of reflections in the group algebras of the exceptional finite reflection groups.

papers.title: An $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling inequality in every dimension
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\geq2$) be measurable with $0<|Ω|<\infty$, and let $u_Ω$ be its logarithmic potential ($N=2$) or Newtonian potential ($N\geq3$), normalized so that $Δu_Ω=χ_Ω$. We prove the sharp inequality \[ \int_Ω|\nabla u_Ω|^2\,\mathrm{d} x \leq\frac{1}{2Nω_{N-1}} \iint_{Ω\timesΩ}\frac{\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} y}{|x-y|^{N-2}}, \] where $ω_{N-1}=|\mathbb{S}^{N-1}|$, with equality if and only if $Ω$ is a ball up to a null set. In dimension two this settles the $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling conjecture of Fleeman and Khavinson. For $N\ge3$ it is equivalent to the scale-free bound that at most the fraction $(N-2)/(2N)$ of the total field energy lies inside $Ω$. We also obtain an explicit deficit identity, a sharp extension to bounded nonnegative densities, and consequences for torsional rigidity, Bergman analytic content, Brownian motion, and aggregation equations.

papers.title: Complete $RO$-Graded Tambara Functor of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ for cyclic groups
papers.abstract: We compute the $RO$-graded Tambara functor of $H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ for every finite cyclic group. We introduce a valuation language for homotopy groups: for prime-power cyclic group equivariant, classes are represented by compatible vertex arrays or by edge arrays. In these coordinates we compute products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms. Then we assemble the results into arbitrary finite cyclic group equivariant case. Besides the computation, we also develop the Tate compression theory, which is used in the computation. The Tate compression diagram cut an equivariant spectra into several layer, which the homotopy group can be describe directly by each layers. From it we also give a filtration for $π_\star(H\underline{\mathbb{Z}})$, compatible with products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms.

papers.title: Sobolev Inequalities Relating Rough Riemannian Metrics to their Distance Functions
papers.abstract: In previous papers, the first named author and E. Bryden explored Sobolev like inequalities relating the norm of a Riemmanian metric $g_1$, in terms of a background Riemannian metric $g_0$, in order to estimate the distance function $d_{g_1}$. Although $|g_1|_{g_0}$ is not the gradient of the distance function $d_{g_1}$, it was shown that a Morrey and Sobolev inequalities hold in their appropriate domains. In this paper we see that these results can be extended to the case where $g_1$ is a Rough Riemannian metric, something roughly analogous to an $L^{\infty}$ metric. We show that the proof of the Morrey and Sobolev inequality go through, with appropriate adjustments, as well as convergence results. We also adapt previous examples from the literature to the rough Riemannian metric case which show the hypotheses from the main theorems are necessary.

papers.title: Bore wave solutions to the viscous Saint-Venant system with capillarity
papers.abstract: We study a traveling wave formulation of the viscous Saint-Venant system in one spatial dimension with capillarity, which can be reduced to an equivalent nonlinear third order ODE. We construct heteroclinic orbits for small positive capillarity, for arbitrary positive capillarity under an explicit small Froude number condition, and in a small-amplitude regime away from the critical Froude number. These then give rise to smooth traveling bore wave solutions to the viscous Saint-Venant system.

papers.title: Width and amplitude inequalities over DG-rings
papers.abstract: We study width over commutative noetherian local differential graded (DG) rings with bounded homology. We establish a derived width formula and prove amplitude inequalities for the derived completion of derived Hom and tensor products. As applications, we obtain Iversen's amplitude inequality and a criterion ensuring that regular sequences on a DG-module are regular on the DG-ring. These applications recover results for DG-modules with finitely generated homology and also hold for derived complete DG-modules. Finally, we characterize Cohen--Macaulay DG-rings by the existence of a bounded derived complete DG-module of finite injective dimension whose amplitude equals that of the DG-ring. This provides a version of Bass' conjecture for derived complete DG-modules.

papers.title: A complete classification of minimal value set polynomials
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of minimal value set polynomials (MVSPs), settling a problem introduced by Carlitz, Lewis, Mills and Straus in 1961. For MVSPs $F \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ with more than two values, earlier work showed that their value sets $\left\{F(a): a \in \mathbb{F}_q\right\}$ can be reduced to the form $\mathcal U^v=\{u^v:u\in \mathcal U\}$, where $\mathcal U$ is a vector space over a subfield of $\mathbb F_q$, and $v\geq 1$ is a suitable integer. This classification proceeds through two parallel constructions, according to whether $\mathcal U$ is itself a field or not, governed respectively by the cyclic multiplicative structure and by the additive linearized structure. In both cases, Hasse derivatives impose constraints on the root multiplicities of a distinguished factor of $F$, leading to a factorization that preserves the underlying structure in a polynomial of smaller degree and thus allows the argument to be iterated.

papers.title: Finite-Sample Optimal Conformal Prediction Sets under Covariate Shift
papers.abstract: We study conformal prediction under covariate shift with a known covariate density ratio, seeking prediction sets with minimum expected length under the target distribution. For every calibration sample size, we prove that the rule combining the inverse conditional-density score with randomized weighted conformal calibration minimizes this expected length among all rules valid over the full weighted-exchangeability class. We approximate the oracle using quantile and kernel histograms, including forest-weighted estimators, and select estimators and tuning parameters by resampling to estimate calibrated target length. On a bounded response domain, we bound excess length linearly in $L^1$ density error at fixed calibration size, without requiring a uniform positive lower bound on the true density. We also bound selection-pool and resampling errors. Under explicit growth conditions, the selected procedure approaches the same oracle while the calibration size remains fixed. Experiments on 36 known-density configurations and four public regression datasets compare coverage, prediction-set length, and runtime with existing methods. In targeted low-coverage and strong-shift comparisons, inverse-density selection yields shorter mean sets in most cases and lower mean runtime than the evaluated weighted baselines, with some differences in achieved coverage.

papers.title: Wasserstein Bounds for Euler and Randomized Midpoint Langevin Sampling with Noisy Gradients
papers.abstract: Stochastic-gradient Langevin methods are sampling algorithms that replace the gradient of the log probability density by a noisy, possibly biased evaluation. We study how such gradient-evaluation errors affect the Euler and randomized midpoint discretizations of Langevin dynamics by comparing each noisy chain with its exact-gradient counterpart. For continuously differentiable, strongly log-concave targets with globally Lipschitz gradients, we derive comparison bounds under a sub-Gaussian condition on the gradient noise. The resulting 2-Wasserstein bounds hold uniformly over iterations, and are linear in both the step size and the $L^2$ norm of the evaluation bias, with a square-root dependence on dimensionality. To the best of our knowledge, no comparable 2-Wasserstein bounds have previously been established for randomized midpoint with noisy gradients. For Euler, our results complement recent Wasserstein bounds by allowing biased evaluations, and by not requiring additional regularity assumptions on the evaluation errors.

papers.title: Optimality of Threshold Policies for Heat Storage Optimization and a Policy Gradient Algorithm
papers.abstract: We study the optimal control of a stylized finite-horizon heat-storage system operated by a prosumer who can buy heat from and sell heat to a district heating network. Heat production and consumption are uncertain, and charging and discharging decisions have to be taken before the subsequent heat balance is observed. The resulting problem is formulated as a Markov decision process with continuous state and action spaces. We first establish a structural characterization of the optimal policy as a two-parameter threshold policy. Under additional regularity assumptions, we prove differentiability and Lipschitz properties of the value functions. Exploiting the threshold structure, we parameterize the policy by the time-dependent lower and upper thresholds and derive a pathwise stochastic-gradient estimator. We then propose a projected stochastic policy-gradient algorithm, establish a constrained Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz inequality and derive global finite-sample bounds for both the objective optimality gap and the distance to the optimal threshold vector. Finally, numerical experiments for a non-stationary heat-balance process illustrate the evolution of the threshold parameters.

papers.title: Spectrahedral relaxations and tightenings of rigidly convex sets
papers.abstract: We construct a natural spectrahedral relaxation of a rigidly convex set (rcs) that depends only on the cubic part and on the degree of the defining real zero polynomial. For quadratic polynomials, we prove exactness and for a product of linear polynomials, we show that a higher order version of our relaxation is exact. We also establish a way of tightening the relaxation by moving the origin inside the rcs, and that the rcs is recovered by sweeping the origin over its interior. To obtain all these results we use a linear form that is closely connected to the zeros of a given real zero polynomial. We also prove that any rcs can be written as an affine linear slice of the cone of non-negative polynomials. Using this, we can define a hierarchy of tightenings that are spectrahedral shadows. We can show that this tightening is exact if the given polynomial admits a determinantal representation. This tightening is similar to a tightening of a hyperbolicity cone due to Kummer, Plaumann, and Vinzant.

papers.title: Ternary analogs of dendriform algebras and quadri-algebras
papers.abstract: We construct ternary analogs of dendriform algebras and quadri-algebras, generalizing the well-known binary case. These new structures are defined in terms of nonsymmetric operads. We construct these new operads using ternary operations defined in terms of ternary Rota-Baxter operators. The relations defining these operads lie in the quadratic subspace of the kernel of a rewriting morphism from a free operad to the operad generated by one associative ternary operation and one (or two commuting) unary operators satisfying the ternary Rota-Baxter relation(s). We use computational algebra to compute a basis for the quadratic component of the kernel and thereby obtain the quadratic relations which define these new operads. In the dendriform case, we obtain 3 operations satisfying 10 relations. In the quadri-algebra case, we obtain 9 operations satisfying 50 relations. The latter computations combine modular and rational arithmetic, but we are able to provide certificates of the results which can be verified in characteristic 0.

papers.title: Finite algebras whose equational probability spectrum contains a big gap
papers.abstract: We classify the finite algebras $\mathbf{A}$ for which there is no value $p$ satisfying $\frac{1}{|A|}<p<1$ in the equational probability spectrum of $\mathbf{A}$. We will use the classification to determine which finite algebras have minimal equational probability spectrum. In our final section, we explore the relationship, for finite algebras, between the properties of (i)~having a finite equational probability spectrum and (ii)~being an abelian algebra.

papers.title: Uniqueness and comparison principle for Trudinger's parabolic equation with Hölder continuous boundary values
papers.abstract: For every $p > 1$, we establish uniqueness and comparison principle for Trudinger's parabolic equation \[ \partial_t (|u|^{p-2}u) = \text{div}(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u) \quad \text{in } Ω\times (0,\text{T}), \] assuming suitable Hölder regularity for the boundary values. Our comparison principle applies to sign-changing weak sub- and supersolutions. As an application, we obtain uniqueness of weak solutions to Cauchy--Dirichlet problems when the lateral boundary data is suitably Hölder continuous in time. In particular, Lipschitz continuous boundary values are covered.

papers.title: Homotopy types and torsion in homology of generalized chessboard complexes
papers.abstract: Multiple chessboard complexes are deleted joins of skeleta of a simplex. We classify their homotopy types for at most three rows and extend this classification to arbitrary column capacities, with the $2$-torus as the only exception to a wedge of spheres. We determine explicit homotopy decompositions for two families with four and five rows and use a common capacity redistribution map to construct infinite families with $2$- and $3$-torsion in integral homology. Together, these results give a negative answer to the Segre part of the problem posed by Reiner and Roberts on characteristic-free resolutions of Segre and Veronese modules and identify three as the largest number of rows for which all generalized chessboard complexes have torsion-free integral homology. Our $3$-torsion construction applies to every square ordinary chessboard complex with at least five rows. Combined with earlier results, it completes the proof of the Shareshian-Wachs conjecture on torsion in chessboard complexes.

papers.title: Quasiisometric embeddings of right-angled Artin groups into products
papers.abstract: We provide obstructions to the existence of quasiisometric embeddings of right-angled Artin groups into products of trees, hyperbolic spaces, and other right-angled Artin groups.

papers.title: The generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, including rigidity in the equality case. As a corollary, we obtain that isoperimetric regions are bounded. We prove the conjecture for Alexandrov spaces with two sided curvature bounds as well. A sharp Michael-Simon-type inequality for hypersurfaces in these spaces is also shown.

papers.title: Stationary integral cycles asymptotic to a pair of oriented $n$-planes in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$
papers.abstract: We prove a uniqueness theorem for stationary integral $n$-cycles asymptotic to a pair of n-planes satisfying the symmetric angle condition. For the general angle condition, we obtain a classification for complete smooth embedded oriented minimal submanifolds with vanishing first de Rham cohomology that are asymptotic to a pair of $n$-planes.

papers.title: Stable limits for the clone-mutant chain with mother-dependent mutation
papers.abstract: We consider the general mother-dependent neutral mutation model defined in Blancas, Fittipaldi and Hernández-Torres (2026), consisting of a multitype branching process in which every individual carries one of $d$ alleles and each mutant child acquires a type different from that of its mother, according to a prescribed distribution. We assume that the total offspring distribution is critical and belongs to the domain of attraction of an $α$-stable law, with $α\in(1,2)$, while mutations are rare. Extending the results of Blancas and Rivero (2018), we prove the finite-dimensional convergence of the rescaled Markov chain that records, in each allelic generation, the sizes of the type-specific clone subfamilies and the mutant populations they produce. The limiting clone masses form a multitype Jiřina process driven by stable subordinators with drift, whose branching mechanism combines the stable reproduction law with the mother-dependent mutation matrix.

papers.title: An alternative variational approach to constrained critical points for nonlinear Schrödinger equations with combined nonlinearities
papers.abstract: We introduce a new variational framework for the study of standing waves for nonlinear Schrödinger equations with combined power nonlinearities. The approach is based on minimizing the mass functional over a set defined by an upper bound on the energy and a lower bound on a nonlinear potential term, rather than minimizing the energy at prescribed mass. This yields a new characterization of the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg optimizer through purely variational constraints. As a consequence, we establish the existence of minimizers for all energy levels below a critical threshold and derive the corresponding Euler--Lagrange equations. These minimizers give rise to standing-wave solutions of the nonlinear Schröedinger equation

papers.title: Characteristic identities for orthogonal quantum matrices: examples
papers.abstract: In this note, we illustrate our recent results regarding structure theory of orthogonal Quantum Matrix algebras \cite{OP-BMW,OP-reciprocal,OP-ortho} using the simplest nontrivial example: the RTT-algebra associated with the canonical orthogonal R-matrix of type $O(3)$ (see, e.g., \cite{FRT}). By introducing a suitable linear order on the set of generators, we obtain a set of quadratic relations defining the algebra. Next, we investigate relations among its higher-degree polynomials. As a result, we verify `in components' the Cayley-Hamilton and the reciprocal relations, obtained earlier with the use of the R-matrix techniques. We explicitly calculate the coefficients of the characteristic polynomials of quantum matrices and propose a conjecture regarding the form of the Hilbert-Poincaré series for the RTT-algebra.

papers.title: Symplectomorphism invariance of the wrapped Fukaya category
papers.abstract: An exact symplectomorphism of finite type Liouville manifolds is called 'strict' if it has bounded primitive; such symplectomorphisms are well known to induce deformation equivalences and hence equivalences of wrapped Fukaya categories. Here we note that an arbitrary symplectomorphism of Weinstein manifolds, with no assumptions at infinity, can be used to construct an equivalence of Fukaya categories. We combine this with a pointwise criterion for constructing such symplectomorphisms to improve two statements in the mirror symmetry literature -- for very affine hypersurfaces and multiplicative hypertoric varieties -- where Fukaya categories were calculated for a Liouville form not known to be strictly exact symplectomorphic to the natural Kähler Liouville form on the space in question. All results are obtained using ChatGPT Astra.

papers.title: Sharp $L^4$ Strichartz estimate for the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$
papers.abstract: We prove the local $L^4$ Strichartz estimate without derivative loss for the Zakharov--Kuznetsov flow on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$. This reaches the sharp spatial regularity endpoint and implies the embedding $X^{0,b}\hookrightarrow L^4$ for every $b>1/2$. The proof reduces the estimate to a semi-algebraic mixed-measure estimate.

papers.title: Flow Matching for Fluctuation-Based Fluorescence Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Fluctuation-based super-resolution techniques are an appealing alternative to single-molecule and structured-illumination microscopy, as they adapt to standard acquisition settings and exploit the independent stochastic fluctuations of fluorophores across a sequence of frames. However, most existing approaches lack an explicit model of the acquisition process and provide only relative intensity estimates, limiting quantitative analyses. In this work, we combine model-based and generative approaches to exploit the full stochastic information in the sequence, proposing a reconstruction framework built on flow matching and a double-Poisson forward model accounting for blinking, blur, under-sampling and noise. The method alternates two steps: a flow matching model first learns the distribution of the acquired data; then, the sample and the background are jointly estimated by minimising a Kullback-Leibler divergence between observed and simulated distributions via regularised proximal gradient steps. On simulated and real Argolight data, the method resolves lines separated by 120 nm, outperforming SACD and eSRRF.

papers.title: Homogenization of degenerate parabolic equations with nonlinear Robin reactions in perforated domains
papers.abstract: We study periodic homogenization of a parabolic equation with linear, degenerate bulk terms in a perforated domain, with a monotone nonlinear Robin reaction of order $\varepsilon$ on the pore walls. The storage coefficient may vanish on sets of positive measure, and the diagonal diffusion weights are not bounded below but satisfy an inverse-integrability condition. Under positivity of the mean storage, a quantitative cell-detection estimate yields strong compactness of the states and of the scaled traces. The effective equation has positive storage, a positive-definite diffusion matrix given by a weighted cell problem, and a nonlinear volume reaction obtained by averaging over the pore surface. We also prove a strong weighted-gradient corrector and uniform-in-time convergence of the dissipated and stored energies and of the states in the storage-weighted $L^2$ norm.

papers.title: Maximal Curves with Few Automorphisms
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of constructing maximal curves with few automorphisms over finite fields. Our main ingredient is the determination of the \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\!\left(\overline{\mathbb F}_p\right)\)-stabilizer of the roots of the Chebyshev polynomials, apart from two exceptional cases already treated in the literature. We prove that, in all other cases, the only nontrivial Möbius symmetry is the sign involution. This settles the general case for the automorphism groups of the corresponding Chebyshev curves. We further construct an infinite family of maximal curves of unbounded genus whose only nontrivial automorphism is the hyperelliptic involution. This reveals a contrasting phenomenon to the common heuristic that curves with many rational points tend to have large automorphism groups.

papers.title: Defining 2-group symmetries on lattices and extracting their anomalies
papers.abstract: Ordinary $0$-form symmetries $G$ can mix with $1$-form symmetries $Π_2$ to form a $2$-group $\mathcal{G}$. We give a concrete lattice definition for a class of finite $2$-group symmetries in terms of local relations among symmetry operators. These relations identify the Postnikov class $[ρ]\in H^3(BG,Π_2)$ that characterizes the mixing. We develop a method to extract anomalies of these symmetries in one spatial dimension by restricting symmetry operations to an interval and comparing their composition near its endpoints. We also construct explicit qubit symmetry actions in $d=1,2,3$ spatial dimensions for a $2$-group with $G=Π_2=\mathbb{Z}_2$. These actions share the same nontrivial Postnikov class but include both anomaly-free and anomalous realizations. Their cohomological anomalies are classified by $H^{d+2}(B\mathcal G,U(1))$, which is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=1,2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=3$, and our constructions realize every class in these dimensions. Our results connect higher-group symmetry and its anomalies to concrete lattice operations, providing a microscopic framework for studying anomalous symmetries.

papers.title: Novel properties of polynomials
papers.abstract: We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for a complex polynomial to have a prescribed multiset of roots, expressed in terms of its coefficients and complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials. These conditions extend the classical Vieta formulas and yield explicit formulas for the coefficients of the corresponding quotient. We apply our results to obtain characterizations of Kronecker polynomials through identities involving symmetric polynomials and construct Borwein multiples of products of cyclotomic polynomials.

papers.title: On the convexity of the fundamental domain of binary cyclotomic forms
papers.abstract: Denote by $Φ_m(X,Y)\in\Z[X,Y]$, $m\geqslant 1$ the sequence of binary cyclotomic forms, so that $Φ_m(T,1)\in\Z[T]$, $m\geqslant 1$ is the sequence of cyclotomic polynomials. We prove that, for $m\geqslant 3$, the fundamental domain $ \cal{O}_m:= \{ (x,y)\in\R^2\; \mid \; Φ_m(x,y)\leqslant 1\} $ of $Φ_m$ is a convex subset of $\R^2$ if and only if $m$ is equal to $p$, $2p$ or $2^k$ with $p$ an odd prime and $k\geqslant 2$. Finally we investigate the convexity of the fundamental domains attached to some products of binary forms $Φ_m$.

papers.title: Nonlinear springs with orbits in radicals: a solvability criterion
papers.abstract: An odd polynomial oscillator has a periodic orbit given by a quadrature. When the zeros of the energy polynomial are all simple or all of even multiplicity, that quadrature is elementary exactly when the polynomial is a perfect square, and the time is a sum of inverse tangents. Recovering the displacement inverts that relation, algebraic when their coefficients are commensurate, making a closed form a Galois question. This paper identifies the group as the monodromy group of a rational map, computes its branch data from the parameters, and shows the branch value at the phase-angle singularity never vanishes, so every decomposition pairs the amplitudes reciprocally. In the commensurate family with distinct real factors, the orbit is radical exactly when the primitive inversion degree is at most four, or when reciprocal pairs leave a reduced spring of that degree. Radical orbits occur at the fifth, ninth, thirteenth and seventeenth force orders, the last only for reciprocal members, an expression recorded for each. The multiplicity hypothesis cannot be dropped. Factoring the energy polynomial into square and squarefree parts turns the quadrature into a differential of the third kind on a hyperelliptic curve, where elementarity is a torsion condition on the divisor of its poles with a vanishing holomorphic remainder. The first nonsquare elementary member appears at the ninth force order, and the power pullback inverts in closed form at every such order, giving a radical orbit for a confining spring of arbitrarily high degree with a sufficient condition for positive coefficients.

papers.title: Pooled Testing under Congestion: Operational Scaling Laws for Pool-Size Selection
papers.abstract: Classical pooled-testing rules choose pool sizes to reduce the number of tests. In practice, however, samples arrive over time, pools take time to form, testing capacity is finite, and positive pools create bursts of follow-up work. These operational features can make the test-efficient pool size far from the delay-efficient one. We formulate pooled testing with stochastic arrivals and finite testing capacity as a queueing system, and derive exact performance representations and asymptotic scaling laws for fixed-batch Dorfman testing and a dynamic two-threshold policy. The analysis reveals three distinct design regimes. When test usage is the main concern, the classical Dorfman rule is recovered and the optimal pool size scales with the inverse square root of prevalence. When delay accumulated while the laboratory is busy testing another batch matters, positive pools create service-time variability that grows more rapidly with pool size than the mean retesting burden, and the optimal scale shifts to the inverse cube root of prevalence. When waiting to assemble a pool is itself costly, the optimal fixed pool size remains bounded even as prevalence becomes very small. Under severe capacity scarcity, congestion remains relevant at the classical Dorfman scale: the square-root law survives, but with a capacity-dependent constant. Dynamic pooling separates two operational decisions that fixed pool sizes conflate. A lower threshold determines when routine testing should begin, while an upper threshold limits pooling when backlog is high. The lower threshold follows the cube-root scale, whereas the upper threshold primarily acts as congestion control. The results show how prevalence, capacity, and delay jointly determine pooling decisions and explain why operationally optimal pools can be much smaller than those suggested by test-efficiency calculations alone.

papers.title: The NWU ageing property of the gamma-gamma distribution
papers.abstract: Baricz et al. [BPV2011] posed the question of whether the $K$-distribution (or gamma-gamma distribution) satisfies the ageing property known as the new is better than used (NBU) property. In this paper we address this question by establishing that, under certain parameter conditions, the gamma-gamma distribution satisfies the new is worse than used (NWU) property rather than the NBU property. For the remaining parameter ranges, we show that the gamma-gamma distribution is neither NBU nor NWU. The proofs rely on tools from the theory of stochastic orders of random variables. Moreover, by exploiting the fact that the random variable that follows the $K$-distribution is actually the product of two independent gamma random variables, we obtain alternative proofs of our results. Similarly, by exploiting the fact that the random variable that follows the beta-prime distribution is actually the quotient of two independent gamma random variables, we establish analogous NBU/NWU properties for this distribution. We also establish sufficient conditions under which the product of two independent positive random variables possesses the NWU and decreasing failure rate (DFR) properties. On the other hand, we show that the survival function of the $K$-distribution is hyperbolically completely monotone by representing it as the Laplace transform of a random variable belonging to the class of generalized gamma convolutions. As a consequence, we establish some monotonicity properties of the Mills ratio and hazard rate function of the $K$-distribution. These results provide further insight into the ageing and monotonicity properties of the gamma-gamma distribution. In addition, we derive a new integral representation and two new series representations, as well as bounds, for the survival function of the $K$-distribution.

papers.title: Moment Polyptychs and the Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric variety of complex dimension $2n$ using symplectic cutting. When the defining arrangement is cooriented so that its base region is non-empty and bounded, fibre rotation has proper moment map and produces compact Kähler orbifold cuts carrying the residual torus action. We introduce the moment polyptych of such a cut, a polytopal complex assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and show that its vertices and local lattice data determine the fixed points, tangent weights, and finite orbifold groups required for equivariant orbifold Riemann-Roch localisation. Even for a smooth hypertoric manifold, a reducible core forces every cut in the outer cut chamber to have non-trivial cyclic isotropy, while the cuts are smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety, which is then a product of projective spaces. For a positive regular integral level $d$ in the outer cut chamber, algebraic cutting identifies the cut's quantisation with a finite filtration piece of the circle-graded quantisation of the original hypertoric variety, whose successive quotients recover the individual circle-weight spaces. We prove that the higher cohomology of the pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes at every such level, so that the localised index is the character of the actual space of sections. Finally, a residual weight $x$ occurs at level $d$ if and only if $\mathcal{S}(x) \leq d$, where $\mathcal{S}$ is the arrangement slack function, with multiplicity $\binom{d - \mathcal{S}(x) + n}{n}$. Thus, each finite stage admits a weighted lattice-point description whose multiplicity function is supported on the lattice points in the support of the level-$d$ moment polyptych.

papers.title: Jacob's ladders and wander from Hardy-Littlewood integral (1918) to the $ζ$-Platonic cube form of equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem
papers.abstract: In this paper we obtain $ζ$-Platonic cube form of our almost linear formula. From this follows, for example, the $ζ$-Platonic equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem. The last result represents the point of contact between the Hardy-Littlewood integral and the Fermat-Wiles theorem and also with one of the Platonic solid - cube.

papers.title: Local-to-Global Theorems Based on Cones with Applications to Graph Coloring
papers.abstract: Local-to-Global theorems are a cornerstone of many of recent developments in theoretical computer science from coding theory and PCPs all the way to analyzing mixing time of Markov chains. Building on trickledown theorems on simplicial complexes, several techniques have been established to obtain tighter local-to-global theorems to analyze the spectral gap of the Glauber dynamics, namely matrix trickledown, ${\mathcal C}$-Lorentzian polynomials and more recently Bochner type inequalities. In this paper, we adopt non-local local-to-global/Bochner type inequalities on "cones", corresponding to the local neighborhood of a given vertex, to show that the Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time to sample proper colorings of maximum degree $Δ$ graphs as long as $q\geq 1.7408Δ$.

papers.title: A short proof of the universality of the fundamental shadow links
papers.abstract: We give a constructive three-dimensional proof of Costantino and Thurston's universality theorem for fundamental shadow links. More precisely, every compact connected oriented three-manifold with empty or toroidal boundary can be obtained by integral Dehn filling along a subset of the boundary components of a fundamental shadow link exterior.

papers.title: Spine extremality and its frequency in critical branching random walks
papers.abstract: We study the generations at which the distinguished spine of a critical branching random walk occupies the spatial minimum. Under finite positive offspring variance and any nonconstant law of independent real edge increments, their number up to generation $N$ is $(\log N)^{1+o(1)}$ almost surely and has order $\log N$ in probability, with ties included. The same conclusions hold for the unique-minimum event. No spatial moment assumption is needed. The proof combines counting estimates from the spine decomposition with uniform control of extremal multiplicity in an ordinary surviving tree. For a selected minimizer, its one-time probability is the ordinary survival probability $q_n$, and recurrence is equivalent to $\sum_nq_n=\infty$. We also exhibit a critical infinite-variance offspring family for which the weak-minimum event occurs only finitely often, for every nonconstant increment law. We determine the polynomial order of its last occurrence and, for Gaussian or Laplace increments, prove quantitative eventual separation of the spine from the minimum. The sharp frequency constant and limiting distribution in the nonconstant finite-variance model remain undetermined.

papers.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities
papers.abstract: We prove a new functional inequality for uniformly log-concave measures, stronger than the Poincaré inequality. This new inequality bounds the variance of differences of convex functions and is motivated by the stability theory of optimal transport: for a fixed uniformly log-concave source measure, it provides a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials with respect to variations of the target measure. Applying this inequality to Gaussian measures, we recover the fact that the Bures-Wasserstein distance between two positive semidefinite matrices is equivalent to the Frobenius distance between their square roots. Our proofs hinge upon linearization arguments for the Monge-Ampère equation governing the quadratic optimal transport problem.

papers.title: Nonuniqueness of Solutions to 2D Incompressible Euler Equations with Unbounded Vorticity
papers.abstract: We construct two distinct solutions of the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation with the same initial vorticity in $\bigcap_{1\le p<\infty}L^p(\mathbb R^2)$. The vorticities are compactly supported in space and have mean zero, so the corresponding velocities have finite energy. The nonuniqueness mechanism is a cascade of transitions in quadrupole dynamics across infinitely many scales.

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles
papers.abstract: We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact Kähler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations. Our proofs build on the purity theorem and descent lemma of Cattani, Kaplan, and Schmid. We extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles. We also establish formal analogs for projective bundle modules over Hodge--Lefschetz modules, with applications to tautological classes and descent on matroid Chow rings.

papers.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
papers.abstract: Weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance in language model pretraining, yet a unified understanding of why such control helps and how much is needed remains incomplete. We analyze norm control in Muon over the entire training trajectory using the \emph{accumulated effective learning rate}, $C_T=\sum_{t<T}η_t/\|W_t\|_F$, where $η_t$ is the nominal learning rate and $η_t/\|W_t\|_F$ is the effective learning rate relative to the weight norm. For bounded update directions, accumulation over any training interval bounds relative weight displacement. We show that vanilla Muon can accumulate only logarithmically, potentially limiting exploration and helping explain its slower empirical progress, whereas MuonW and MuonH guarantee at least linear accumulation under the stated conditions. Going beyond bounded-norm control, we show that sufficiently slow norm growth guarantees faster accumulation than the logarithmic worst case, opening up less restrictive optimizer designs. Based on this insight, we propose MuonGS, which uses Gram--Schmidt (GS) projection to remove the radial component of each Muon update without fixing the weight norm. With bounded update directions and a constant nominal learning rate, we prove that the weight norm grows at most proportionally to $\sqrt{t}$ after $t$ steps. Consequently, MuonGS guarantees $C_T=Ω(\sqrt{T})$, with accumulation sustained even in later training. Further, for smooth scale-invariant objectives we establish its $O(T^{-1/2})$ stationarity guarantee. In pretraining experiments with 160M- and 400M-parameter dense models as well as a 135M active- and 1B total- parameter MoE model, MuonGS achieves lower validation perplexity than MuonH at long training horizons. In particular, for the dense model it achieves an estimated token-equivalent speedup up to about $15\%$ at matched validation loss to MuonH.

papers.title: Applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles: ODEs, PDEs, integer and difference equations
papers.abstract: Mappings contracting perimeters of triangles are Banach contractions whenever every point of the underlying metric space is an accumulation point. Consequently, applying the perimeter-contraction theorem on a complete metric space without isolated points yields an existence result already covered by Banach's fixed point theorem. This observation applies, in particular, to operators associated with differential and integral equations acting on standard nontrivial function spaces, such as spaces of continuous functions $C[a,b]$, Lebesgue spaces $L_p$, and Sobolev spaces $W^{k,p}$, equipped with their usual norm metrics. Thus, applications extending beyond Banach's theorem for the same operator and metric require a complete invariant domain containing some number of isolated points. Such a domain may be a closed subset of a standard function space, despite the absence of isolated points in the ambient space. The main goal of this paper is to illustrate applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles in settings where the associated operators are not Banach contractions. The differential-equation examples admit interpretations as stylized models combining continuous evolution, nonlocal measurement, and quantized feedback. The integer and difference-equation examples illustrate the effects of rounding on equilibria and periodic responses.

papers.title: Algebraic fiberings of right-angled Coxeter groups on bipartite cone graphs
papers.abstract: We study systems of moves and states in the sense of [JNW21] on certain bipartite graphs, and the associated homomorphisms from the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups to $\mathbb Z$. We give examples of right-angled Coxeter groups whose graphs do not satisfy the legal system criterion, but contain finite index right-angled Coxeter subgroups whose graphs admit legal systems. We also provide a family of examples of graphs without legal systems, where no sequence of the considered graph operations yields a graph with a legal system. Moreover, we show that for a bipartite graph and an orbit of non-empty states under the bipartite system of moves, the associated homomorphism from the commutator subgroup of the right-angled Coxeter group to $\mathbb Z$ has finitely generated kernel if and only if the system is legal.

papers.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP I: The shock region
papers.abstract: We investigate the role of asymmetry in the stationary measures of integrable probabilistic models with boundary interactions. This paper is the first in a series of three focusing on the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP). The stationary measure of open ASEP admits a two-layer Gibbs representation in which a correction term, which we call the Bryc polynomial, encodes the dependence on the asymmetry parameter. We give a probabilistic interpretation of the Bryc polynomial in terms of a birth-death-type Markov chain. As an application, we obtain sharp total variation approximations of the stationary measure by Bernoulli product measures in the high- and low-density phases of the shock region. These approximations yield further applications, including moderate deviation estimates for the stationary measure of open ASEP, as well as asymptotic results for the related model of open ASEP with light particles.

papers.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP II: The coexistence line
papers.abstract: We study the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on the coexistence line. Our starting point is Bryc's two-layer Gibbs representation, together with the probabilistic interpretation, established in the first paper in this series, of the associated Bryc polynomial in terms of an inhomogeneous birth--death chain. Our main result gives a sharp approximation of the stationary measure. Specifically, we identify the shock location as an explicit observable of the particle configuration and obtain optimal bounds on the total variation distance between its law and the uniform measure on the lattice. Conditional on the shock location, we approximate, in total variation distance, the joint law of the occupation variables away from the shock by Bernoulli product measures with different densities to its left and right. These approximations lead to further applications, including fluctuation limits, moderate deviation bounds for the particle density, and limits for correlation functions under the stationary measure.

papers.title: Approximate Counting for Mixed $p$-Spin Glasses in Weak External Fields via Cluster Expansion
papers.abstract: We give algorithms for approximating the partition function $Z_N$ of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) model and finite mixed Ising $p$-spin models with $p\ge 3$. The algorithms apply at a fixed margin below the second-moment threshold $β_{\mathrm f}$ with homogeneous weak external fields $|h|\leqρ_0N^{-1/4}$, for fixed $ρ_0>0$. For any accuracy $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and failure parameter $δ\in(0,1)$, they approximate $\log Z_N$ to additive error $\varepsilon$. The number of exact operations is polynomial jointly in $N$, $\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $δ^{-1}$. The disorder variables have i.i.d symmetric distribution with unit variance. The failure probability is at most $δ$ plus an explicit disorder tail bound. This tail bound tends to zero under a finite fourth moment condition. Our approach builds on the cluster expansions of Aizenman--Lebowitz--Ruelle~\cite{ALR87} and Dey--Wu~\cites{DW23,DW26}. For higher-order mixtures, we retain hypergraphs using few vertices and evaluate their total weight deterministically through local spin averages and inclusion--exclusion. For SK, we impose cutoffs on the number of vertices of degree at least three and on the total number of edges. We estimate the retained sum using randomized color coding~\cite{AYZ95}. A lower tail control based on reverse hypercontractivity~\cite{MOS13} converts the mean-square approximation of the normalized partition function into logarithmic accuracy.

papers.title: Lower- and upper-$C^2$ integrands: a structured class of functions for stochastic nonconvex optimization
papers.abstract: We study nonconvex stochastic functions that admit a structured second-order representation, a generalization of lower- and upper-$C^2$ functions to normal integrands. Similarly to the deterministic case, lower-$C^2$ normal integrands are defined as the pointwise maxima over a compact random index set of functions that are twice-continuously differentiable in the decision variable with an integrable bounded Hessian. Our main result is a local value function characterization of this class of functions, namely, that they satisfy a local sufficient ascent property almost surely. Equivalently, they differ from a convex normal integrand by a random quadratic. The upper-$C^2$ theory follows by a change of sign, and delivers the corresponding lower envelopes, the form in which these integrands appear as second-stage value functions of stochastic programs with compact recourse. We also show that for this class integrability of the function values, of the local Lipschitz moduli, and of the minimum-norm Clarke subgradients are equivalent. We then study smooth integrands, finite lower envelopes, difference-of-convex integrands, Moreau and forward--backward envelopes, compositions with a smooth map, monotone convex compositions, and compact-recourse stochastic programs within these classes of nonconvex stochastic functions. As an application, we show that the optimistic loss of partial-label regression and the variational formulation of the conditional value-at-risk fit within this framework.

papers.title: Localization, cobordism, and twisted $χ_y$-genera of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$
papers.abstract: We use the method of equivariant localization to obtain a recursion for the cobordism-valued one-point psi-class intersections on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$, and hence the cobordism classes $[\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}]$. Restricting to the hyperbolic formal group law, we recover the Poincaré polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ as a special case, and obtain new formulas for Hirzebruch $χ_y$-genera of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ twisted by tautological line bundles.

papers.title: Shape exclusion for diffusion-limited aggregation
papers.abstract: For diffusion-limited aggregation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 2$, we rule out convergence in volume to bounded regions with boundary measure zero. Moreover, the number of boundary edges grows linearly. For Euclidean DLA in dimensions $2$, $3$, $8$, and $24$, we prove an analogous shape exclusion.

papers.title: Diffusive-dispersive traveling waves and kinetic relations. Generic flux with multiple inflection points
papers.abstract: We consider the broad class of scalar hyperbolic conservation laws with generic non-convex fluxes, which may thus have an arbitrary finite number of inflection points. We investigate the properties of classical and nonclassical shock waves realized as traveling-wave limits of a linear diffusive-dispersive regularization and provide a phase-plane classification beyond the case of a single inflection point. Within the speed range of the generalized Maxwell construction, our main result classifies the left outgoing profiles by their limiting equilibria. In an elementary bowtie configuration, we prove the existence of nonclassical shock profiles with arbitrarily many oscillations. For nested configurations, we order the saddle connections on each entry interval, taking account of inaccessible saddles. We show that the number of oscillations present in the non-classical shock depends on the diffusion-dispersion ratio, and tends to infinity along the elementary families of saddle connections as this ratio tends to zero. Our construction is based on a generalization of Maxwell's equal area rule, which provides us with an invariant region in the phase space for the study of diffusive-dispersive traveling waves.

papers.title: Linear-quadratic mean field games with Volterra dynamics
papers.abstract: We study a class of linear-quadratic mean field games in which the state of each agent follows a stochastic Volterra equation of convolution type. The resulting dynamics are non-Markovian and account for memory effects through a completely monotone kernel, while the mean field interaction enters both the drift and diffusion coefficients. Exploiting a Markovian lifting of the Volterra dynamics, which restores the Markov property at the price of moving to an infinite-dimensional state space, we characterize the optimal response of a representative agent for a given population mean through a system of Riccati equations in Banach spaces, thereby obtaining a feedback representation of the optimal control. We then study the consistency condition defining the mean field equilibrium, which reduces to a forward-backward fixed point equation for the equilibrium mean: we prove existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium on short horizons and, when the control does not act on the diffusion coefficient, on arbitrary horizons under a monotonicity condition on the interaction. Finally, we consider the corresponding finite-player game and establish a quantitative propagation of chaos result. As a consequence, the feedback control of any mean field equilibrium, when implemented by each agent on its own state, yields an $\varepsilon_N$-Nash equilibrium for the $N$-player game, with an explicit rate as the number of agents tends to infinity.

papers.title: Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP III: The fan region
papers.abstract: We study the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) in the fan region with general boundary rates. The stationary height fluctuations in the maximal current phase and on its boundaries within the fan region are known to have limits involving Brownian excursions or meanders. We establish discrete counterparts of these limits: on intervals away from the boundaries, the joint law of the occupation variables is approximated in total variation distance by particle configurations constructed from lazy simple random walk excursions and meanders. In the high- and low-density phases of the fan region, we establish Bernoulli product approximations with errors that decay exponentially in the distance from the relevant boundary. Our methods combine refined combinatorial estimates for Motzkin paths and the matrix product ansatz in the totally asymmetric case with a Fourier-type decomposition (based on Askey--Wilson polynomials) of the change of measure for general asymmetry. In addition, in the maximal current phase and on its boundaries within the fan region, we prove moderate deviation estimates for particle counts on arbitrary sets of sites. These estimates rely on a covariance identity for an auxiliary path measure, through which total nonnegativity (of order two) of the matrices yields negative correlations.

papers.title: Stationary measures of the open KPZ equation: A short proof
papers.abstract: In this note, we give a short probabilistic proof of the two-layer Brownian representation of the stationary measure of the open Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation on a finite interval with arbitrary Neumann boundary parameters, conjectured by Barraquand and Le Doussal and recently established in full generality by Dunlap, Gu and Rosati. Our starting point is Bryc's two-layer Gibbs representation of the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) under Liggett's condition, together with our previously established probabilistic interpretation of the associated Bryc polynomials in terms of inhomogeneous birth--death Markov chains. Martingale estimates yield uniform asymptotics for these polynomials under weakly asymmetric scaling. Combined with known convergence results from open ASEP to open KPZ, these estimates recover the stationary height profile of the open KPZ equation as the first marginal of a reweighted pair of Brownian motions.

papers.title: Generic tensor products are not maximal
papers.abstract: We construct tensor products of uniform matroids which are strictly freer than their generic linear tensor products. In particular, the generic tensor product of two copies of $U_{7,9}$ is not maximal. More generally, for every $a,b\ge2$, this holds for $U_{7,a+7}$ and $U_{7,b+7}$. The construction disproves the uniform tensor-product formulation of Mason's conjecture. Its dual is a relaxation of an explicit circuit-hyperplane of a generic birigidity matroid. By the author's representability theorem, the resulting matroids are non-representable over every field.
