papers.abstract: Our GBDT (generalised Bäcklund-Darboux transformation) approach is used to construct explicit solutions of the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation in the case of the exponential seed $a \exp\{2 i (cx +dt)\}$. The corresponding Baker-Akhiezer functions and evolution of the Weyl functions are obtained as well. In particular, the solutions, which appear in the study of rogue waves, step-like solutions and $N$-modulation solutions of the NLS equation are considered. This work is an essential development of our joint work with Rien Kaashoek and Israel Gohberg, where the seed was trivial, as well as several other of our previous works.

papers.title: StablePCA: Distributionally Robust Learning of Shared Representations from Multi-Source Data
papers.abstract: When synthesizing multi-source high-dimensional data, a key objective is to extract low-dimensional representations that effectively approximate the original features across different sources. Such representations facilitate the discovery of transferable structures and help mitigate systematic biases such as batch effects. We introduce Stable Principal Component Analysis (StablePCA), a distributionally robust framework for constructing stable latent representations by maximizing the worst-case explained variance over multiple sources. A primary challenge in extending classical PCA to the multi-source setting lies in the nonconvex rank constraint, which renders the StablePCA formulation a nonconvex optimization problem. To overcome this challenge, we conduct a convex relaxation of StablePCA and develop an efficient Mirror-Prox algorithm to solve the relaxed problem, with global convergence guarantees. Since the relaxed problem generally differs from the original formulation, we further introduce a data-dependent certificate to assess how well the algorithm solves the original nonconvex problem and establish the condition under which the relaxation is tight. Finally, we explore alternative distributionally robust formulations of multi-source PCA based on different loss functions.

papers.title: Geometric construction of Kashiwara crystals on multiparameter persistence
papers.abstract: We establish a geometric construction of Kashiwara crystals on the irreducible components of the varieties of multiparameter persistence modules. Our approach differs from the seminal work of Kashiwara and Saito, as well as subsequent related works, by emphasizing commutative relations rather than preprojective relations for a given quiver. Furthermore, we provide explicit descriptions of the Kashiwara operators in the fundamental cases of 1- and 2-parameter persistence modules, offering concrete insights into the crystal structure in these settings.

papers.title: Infinite unrestricted sumsets in subsets of abelian groups with large density
papers.abstract: Let $(G,+)$ be a countable abelian group such that the subgroup $\{g+g\colon g\in G\}$ has finite index and the doubling map $g\mapsto g+g$ has finite kernel. We establish lower bounds on the upper density of a set $A\subset G$ with respect to an appropriate Følner sequence, so that $A$ contains a sumset of the form $\{t+b_1+b_2\colon b_1,b_2\in B\}$ or $\{b_1+b_2\colon b_1,b_2\in B\}$, for some infinite $B\subset G$ and some $t\in G$. Both assumptions on $G$ are necessary for our results to be true. We also characterize the Følner sequences for which this is possible. Finally, we show that our lower bounds are optimal in a strong sense.

papers.title: Efficient Algorithms for Isogeny Computation on Hyperelliptic Curves: Their Applications in Post-Quantum Cryptography
papers.abstract: We present e cient algorithms for computing isogenies between hyperelliptic curves, leveraging higher genus curves to enhance cryptographic protocols in the post-quantum context. Our algorithms reduce the computational complexity of isogeny computations from O(g4) to O(g3) operations for genus 2 curves, achieving significant ciency gains over traditional elliptic curve methods. Detailed pseudocode and comprehensive complexity analyses demonstrate these improvements both theoretically and empirically. Additionally, we provide a thorough security analysis, including proofs of resistance to quantum attacks such as Shor's and Grover's algorithms. Our findings establish hyperelliptic isogeny-based cryptography as a promising candidate for secure and e cient post-quantum cryptographic systems.

papers.title: A spanning tree model for chromatic homology
papers.abstract: After the discovery of Khovanov homology, which categorifies the Jones polynomial, an analogous categorification of the chromatic polynomial, known as chromatic homology, was introduced. Its graded Euler characteristic recovers the chromatic polynomial. In this paper, we present a spanning tree model for the chromatic complex, i.e., we describe a chain complex generated by certain spanning trees of the graph that is chain homotopy equivalent to the chromatic complex. We employ the spanning tree model over $\mathcal{A}_m:= \frac{\mathbb{Z}[x]}{<x^m>}$ algebra to answer two open questions. First, we establish the conjecture posed by Sazdanovic and Scofield regarding the homological span of chromatic homology over $\mathcal{A}_m$ algebra, demonstrating that for any graph $G$ with $v$ vertices and $b$ blocks, the homological span is $v - b$. Additionally, we prove a conjecture of Helme-Guizon, Przytycki, and Rong concerning the existence of torsion of order dividing $m$ in chromatic homology over $\mathcal{A}_m$ algebra.

papers.title: Quasi-ribbon but non-ribbon surface-link of trivial components
papers.abstract: An operation on a surface-link preserving the surface-knot components called a quasi-equivalence is introduced, which induces an equivalence relation on the surface-links. A quasi-ribbon surface-link is a surface-link quasi-equivalent to a ribbon surface-link. It is shown that a surface-link of trivial components is a quasi-ribbon surface link if it has only at most one non-spherical component, whereas there exist examples that are not quasi-ribbon surface-links of trivial components when it has at least two aspherical components. For every closed disconnected, orientable surface, a quasi-ribbon but non-ribbon surface-link of trivial components is constructed. This construction is done by applying a positive solution to Cochran's conjecture, meaning that the sphere-knot obtained from the anti-parallel sphere-link of every non-ribbon sphere-knot by surgery along an s-nontrivial or s-trivial fusion 1-handle is a non-ribbon or trivial sphere-knot, respectively.

papers.title: On quaternionic analysis and a certain generalized fractal-fractional $ψ$-Fueter operator
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator in the quaternionic context inspired by the concepts of proportional derivative and Hausdorff derivative ({fractal derivative}) of a function with respect to a fractal measure. Moreover, we establish the corresponding Stokes and Borel-Pompeiu formulas associated to this generalized fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator with respect to a vector valued function induced by truncated exponential functions.

papers.title: Comparing classical tilting modules and $τ$-tilting modules
papers.abstract: We characterize support $τ$-tilting modules as classical tilting modules over quotient algebras satisfying a tensor-vanishing condition, and characterize classical tilting modules as $τ$-tilting modules satisfying a ${\rm Tor}^1$-vanishing condition. We use delooping levels to study \emph{Self-orthogonal $τ$-tilting Conjecture}: any self-orthogonal $τ$-tilting module is classical tilting. We confirm the conjecture when the endomorphism algebra of the module has finite global delooping level.

papers.title: Positive semidefiniteness of $h$-Shuhan matrices (analogs of Borcherds Cartan matrices) and associated determinant sequences
papers.abstract: We introduce an $h$-Shuhan matrix as a real square matrix $H=(h_{ij})$ with a common diagonal entry $h\ge0$, nonpositive integral off-diagonal entries, and the following Cartan-type condition on each unordered pair $\{i,j\}$: either $h_{ij}=h_{ji}$, or $\max\{h_{ij},h_{ji}\}=-1$ and $\min\{h_{ij},h_{ji}\}\le -2$. These conditions imply that the scalar shift $H+(2-h)I_n$ is a generalized Cartan matrix; not every generalized Cartan matrix arises from an $h$-Shuhan matrix in this way. We classify, for $0\le h<2$, all indecomposable $h$-Shuhan matrices that are positive semidefinite, generalized positive semidefinite, or virtual positive semidefinite (the last notion means that all principal minors are nonnegative). For $h<2$, virtual positive semidefiniteness forces $H+(2-h)I_n$ to be of finite Cartan type, the positive-type case of Vinberg's trichotomy (1971). At $h=2$, we describe the boundary case in terms of finite and affine Cartan matrices. The associated determinant recurrences hold for general $h$. We study congruences for integral $h$ and asymptotic and Fibonacci-type identities for $h>2$.

papers.title: Introducing irrational enumeration: analytic combinatorics for objects of irrational size
papers.abstract: We extend the scope of analytic combinatorics to classes containing objects that have irrational sizes. The generating function for such a class is a power series that admits irrational exponents (which we call a Ribenboim series). A transformation then yields a generalised Dirichlet series from which the asymptotics of the coefficients can be extracted by singularity analysis using an appropriate Tauberian theorem. In practice, the asymptotics can often be determined directly from the original generating function. We illustrate the technique with a variety of applications, including tilings with tiles of irrational area, ordered integer factorizations, lattice walks enumerated by Euclidean length, and plane trees with vertices of irrational size. We also explore phase transitions in the asymptotics of families of irrational combinatorial classes. This revision contains corrections to the statement and proof of Theorem 1, to the statement of Conjecture 6, and to the proof of Proposition 13 that appear in the published version.

papers.title: Sharp Estimates for Jacobi Heat Kernels in Double Conic Domains
papers.abstract: We study the even and odd Jacobi heat kernels defined in the context of the multidimensional double cone and its surface, the multidimensional hyperboloid and its surface, and the multidimensional paraboloid and its surface. By integrating the framework of Jacobi polynomials on these domains, as analyzed by Xu, with contemporary methods developed by Nowak, Sjögren, and Szarek for obtaining sharp estimates of the spherical heat kernel, we establish genuinely sharp estimates for the even and odd Jacobi heat kernel in the double conic settings, and for the even Jacobi heat kernel on hyperbolic settings. We also discuss the limitations encountered in extending these results to the remaining settings.

papers.title: Polynomial and Hyperplane Avoidance over the Integers with Applications to Integer-Point Counting
papers.abstract: We study the \emph{Polynomial Avoidance Problem}: given a finite collection $F \subseteq Z[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ of nonzero polynomials, find a vector $x \in Z^n$ of minimum $\ell_p$-norm such that $f(x)\neq0$ for every $f \in F$. Each polynomial is given sparsely as a list of its nonzero terms. The affine special case is the \emph{Hyperplane Avoidance Problem}. This special case arises in Barvinok-type algorithms for counting integer points in polyhedra, when certain rational generating functions must be evaluated at a removable singularity. Our main results are as follows: 1) Let $D:=\sum_{f\in F} \text{deg} f$. Every instance admits a feasible vector $x$ satisfying \[ \|x\|_1 \leq \min\left\{D,\frac{D+n}{2}\right\}. \] This bound is tight. Such a vector can be found by a deterministic algorithm whose bit complexity is polynomial in $D$ and the sparse encoding length of the input. Our proof uses a new algorithmic variant of the \emph{Combinatorial Nullstellensatz}; 2) In the affine case, with $m$ input polynomials, such a vector can be constructed by a fast deterministic polynomial-time algorithm using $O(nm)$ arithmetic operations. For the homogeneous case, Barvinok's original approach provides only the weaker guarantee $\|x\|_1 = O((nm)^{n-1})$; 3) The problem is NP-hard for every $p\in R_{\geq 1}\cup\{\infty\}$, even for homogeneous linear forms; 4) As an application, we improve the complexity bound for counting integer points in general rational polytopes. We also improve the bound for polyhedra of bounded codimension; this includes the counting version of the \emph{Unbounded Subset-Sum} problem as a special case.

papers.title: Eigenspaces of Coleman's Trace Operator
papers.abstract: The Coleman power series defined on a Lubin--Tate tower of extensions over $K$ are compatible with respect to two formal group laws: the multiplicative formal group law and some Lubin--Tate formal group law defined over $\mathcal{O}_K$. We ask if it is possible to generalize Coleman series in order to find series which are compatible with respect to any two Lubin--Tate formal group laws in the same way. We provide a precise formulation of this question and a partial answer towards the classification of all such power series that involves the eigenspaces of Coleman's trace operator. Some additional eigenspaces of Coleman's trace operator are also introduced. These new eigenspaces are used to construct certain fixed points of the $ψ$-operator on the family of trianguline dihedral $(\varphi, Γ)$-modules.

papers.title: Admissible groups over number fields
papers.abstract: Given a field $K$, one may ask which finite groups are Galois groups of field extensions $L/K$ such that $L$ is a maximal subfield of a division algebra with center $K$. Such a group is called admissible over $K$. This connection between inverse Galois theory and division algebras was first explored by Schacher in the 1960s. In this manuscript we consider this problem when $K$ is a number field. For the case when $L/K$ is tamely ramified, we give a complete classification of number fields for which every solvable Sylow-metacyclic group is admissible, extending J. Sonn's result for $K = \mathbb{Q}$. For the case when $L/K$ is allowed to be wildly ramified, we give a characterization of admissible groups over several classes of number fields, and partial results in other cases.

papers.title: Silent Orbits and Cancellations in the Wave Trace
papers.abstract: This paper shows that the wave trace of a bounded and strictly convex planar domain may be arbitrarily smooth in a neighborhood of some point in the length spectrum. In other words, the Poisson relation, which asserts that the singular support of the wave trace is contained in the closure of $\pm$ the length spectrum, can almost be made into a strict inclusion. To do so, we construct large families of domains for which there exist multiple periodic billiard orbits having the same length but different Maslov indices. Using the microlocal Balian-Bloch-Zelditch parametrix for wave invariants developed in our previous paper, we solve a large system of equations for the boundary curvature jets, which leads to the required cancellations. We call such periodic orbits silent, since they are undetectable from the ostensibly audible wave trace. Such cancellations show that there are potential limitations in using the wave trace for inverse spectral problems and, more fundamentally, that the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum are inherently different mathematical objects, at least insofar as the wave trace is concerned.

papers.title: On Hölder continuity and $p^\mathrm{th}$-variation function of Weierstrass-type functions
papers.abstract: We study Hölder continuity, $p^\mathrm{th}$-variation function and Riesz variation of Weierstrass-type functions along the sequence of b-adic partitions, where b>1 is an integer. By a Weierstrass-type function, we mean that in the definition of the well-known Weierstrass function, the power function is replaced by a submultiplicative function, and the Lipschitz continuous cosine and sine functions are replaced by a general periodic Hölder continuous function.

papers.title: Logic-Based Benders Decomposition for Time Slot Management with Mixed Logit Demand
papers.abstract: This paper develops an exact solution framework for the choice-based time slot management problem under mixed logit demand in attended home delivery systems. The problem jointly optimizes delivery slot offerings, price discounts, and routing decisions, with customer choices endogenously modeled through a simulation-based mixed logit formulation embedded via sample average approximation, resulting in a large-scale stochastic mixed-integer program. To address this complexity, we propose a logic-based Benders decomposition (LBBD) that separates strategic assortment and pricing decisions, together with customer choice, from scenario-specific vehicle routing subproblems. We derive problem-specific optimality cuts that exploit the routing structure to provide stronger bounds than generic cuts, and establish their validity. To enhance computational performance, we introduce and systematically evaluate several strengthening strategies, including relaxation-based cut generation and capacity- and flow-based valid inequalities. We further compare two equivalent encodings of the embedded choice model and show that the relative value of each strengthening strategy depends on the strength of the master formulation it complements. Computational experiments on benchmark instances show that the proposed framework significantly extends the range of solvable instances compared to direct MILP approaches. The framework is exact: it converges to a proven optimal solution given sufficient time, and the bounds it produces at intermediate iterations are valid. Within a 12-hour limit, proven optimality is reached for instances with up to 10 customers, and valid bounds are obtained up to 40 customers, including sizes at which the direct MILP formulation returns no feasible solution.

papers.title: Chordal matroids arising from generalized parallel connections II
papers.abstract: In 1961, Dirac showed that chordal graphs are exactly the graphs that can be constructed from complete graphs by a sequence of clique-sums. In an earlier paper, by analogy with Dirac's result, we introduced the class of $GF(q)$-chordal matroids as those matroids that can be constructed from projective geometries over $GF(q)$ by a sequence of generalized parallel connections across projective geometries over $GF(q)$. Our main result showed that when $q=2$, such matroids have no induced minor in $\{M(C_4),M(K_4)\}$. In this paper, we show that the class of $GF(2)$-chordal matroids coincides with the class of binary matroids that have none of $M(K_4)$, $M^*(K_{3,3})$, or $M(C_n)$ for $n\geq 4$ as a flat. We also show that $GF(q)$-chordal matroids can be characterized by an analogous result to Rose's 1970 characterization of chordal graphs as those that have a perfect elimination ordering of vertices.

papers.title: On the rank of the double cohomology of moment-angle complexes
papers.abstract: In [6], the authors construct a cochain complex $C\!H^*(\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}})$ on the cohomology of a moment-angle complex $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}}$ and call the resulting cohomology the double cohomology, $H\!H^*(\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}})$. In this paper, we study the change of rank in double cohomology after gluing an $n$-simplex to a simplicial complex $\mathcal{K}$ in certain conditions. As an application, we give a positive answer to an open problem in [6]: For any even integer $r$, there always exists a simlicial complex $\mathcal{K}$ such that $\operatorname{rank} H\!H^*(\mathcal{Z}_{\mathcal{K}})=r$.

papers.title: Spectrum in alternative topological algebras and a new look at old theorems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider real and complex algebras as well as algebras over general fields. In Section 2, we revisit and prove several results on (quadratic) algebras over general fields. As an example, we demonstrate that a quadratic algebra over a field of characteristic not $2$ is flexible if and only if it is proper--a concept introduced in this paper. In Section 3, we show how to develop the spectral theory in the context of complex (resp. real) one-sided alternative topological algebras. Along the way, spectral theory is used to prove several topological counterparts of the well-known theorems of Frobenius, Hurwitz, Gelfand-Mazur, and Zorn. This is done, for example, in the context of left (resp. right) alternative topological algebras whose duals separate their elements. In Section 4, we consider real and complex algebras in various topological settings and reconsider and prove several results. For instance, it is shown that given a $ 1 < k \in \mathbb{N}$, on any locally complex algebra, there exists a unique nonzero vector space norm, say, $\|.\|$, satisfying the identity $\|a^k\| = \|a\|^k$ on the algebra. In Section 5, among other things, we revisit and slightly strengthen the celebrated theorems of Frobenius, Zorn, Gelfand-Mazur, and Hurwitz, and also give slight extensions of their topological counterparts, e.g., theorems of Albert, Kaplansky, and Urbanik-Wright to name a few, in several

papers.title: Data-driven Wasserstein distributionally robust generalized Nash equilibrium problems with heterogeneous uncertainty
papers.abstract: We study stochastic generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems with heterogeneous, stochastic uncertainty in the cost functions. To address the distributional uncertainty, we let each agent construct an individual Wasserstein ambiguity set around an empirical distribution obtained from private data. We establish finite-sample robustness guarantees for any distributionally robust (DR) GNE. Focusing on variational equilibria, we derive a DR variational inequality (VI) reformulation and establish asymptotic consistency with the nominal stochastic game. Under mild conditions, we derive an exact finite-dimensional generalized Nash equilibrium reformulation. We then quantify how heterogeneous worst-case distributions affect monotonicity, and derive conditions for uniqueness and equilibrium sensitivity. To compute a variational DR GNE, we propose an inexact projected method and establish convergence under vanishing oracle errors, an asymptotic error bound under bounded oracle errors, and linear convergence under exact oracle evaluations.

papers.title: The Einstein-Hilbert functional and the Donaldson-Futaki invariant
papers.abstract: Given a Kaehler manifold polarised by a holomorphic ample line bundle, we consider the circle bundle associated to the polarisation with the induced transversal holomorphic structure. The space of contact structures compatible with this transversal structure is naturally identified with a bundle, of infinite rank, over the space of Kaehler metrics in the first Chern class of the polarisation. We show that the Einstein-Hilbert functional of the associated Tanaka-Webster connections is a functional on this bundle, whose critical points are constant scalar curvature Sasaki structures. In particular, when the group of automorphisms is discrete, these critical points correspond to constant scalar curvature Kaehler metrics in the first Chern class of the polarisation. We show that the Einstein--Hilbert functional satisfies some monotonicity properties along some one-parameter families of CR-contact structures that are naturally associated to test configurations, and that its limit on the central fibre of a test configuration is related to the Donaldson-Futaki invariant through an expansion in terms of an extra real parameter. As a by-product, we obtain an original proof that the existence of constant scalar curvature Kaehler metrics on a polarized manifold implies K-semistability. We also show that the limit of the Einstein-Hilbert functional on the central fibre coincides with the ratio of the equivariant index characters pole coefficients of the central fibre.

papers.title: Epsilon-Identifiability of Causal Quantities
papers.abstract: Identifying the effects of causes and causes of effects is vital in virtually every scientific field. Often, however, the needed probabilities may not be fully identifiable from the available data sources. This paper shows how approximate identifiability is still possible for several probabilities of causation. We term this epsilon-identifiability and demonstrate its usefulness in cases where the behavior of certain subpopulations can be restricted within sufficiently narrow bounds. In particular, we show how unidentifiable causal effects and counterfactual probabilities can be epsilon-identified when such allowances are made. Often, these allowances are easily measured and reasonably assumed. Finally, epsilon-identifiability is applied to the unit selection problem.

papers.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 10: Type-2 isomorphic $C_{np^3}(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = $p$ and related groups
papers.abstract: This article is the $10^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}. In this part, we obtain families of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs $C_{np^3}(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = $p$, and related Abelian groups where $p$ is a prime number and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Theorems \ref{c1} and \ref{c4} are the main results. In Theorem \ref{c4}, it is proved that for $i$ = 1 to $p$, circulant graphs $C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i)$ are isomorphic of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = $p$ and they form Abelian group $(T2_{np^3,p}(C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i)), \circ)$ where $T2_{np^3,p}(C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i))$ = $\{θ_{np^3,p,jn}(C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i))$ = $C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_{i+j}) :$ $j$ = $0,1,...,p-1$ and $i+j$ in $C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_{i+j})$ is calculated under addition modulo $p \}$, $1 \leq x \leq p-1$, $0 \leq y \leq np - 1$, $1 \leq x+yp \leq np^2-1$, $y\in\mathbb{N}_0$, $p,np^3-p\in R^{np^3,x+yp}_i$ and $i,n,x\in\mathbb{N}$. Using Theorem \ref{c4}, a list of $T2_{np^3,p}(C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i))$, each containing $p$ isomorphic circulant graphs $C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i)$ of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = $p$, for $p$ = 3,5,7, $n$ = 1,2 and $y$ = 0 is given in the Annexure and more such families of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs are presented in \cite{v24}.

papers.title: Response time central-limit and failure rate estimation for stationary periodic rate monotonic real-time systems
papers.abstract: Real-time systems consist of a set of tasks, a scheduling policy, and a system architecture, all constrained by timing requirements. Many everyday embedded systems, within devices such as airplanes, cars, trains, and spatial probes, operate as real-time systems. To ensure safe failure rates, response times-the time required for the exection of a task-must be bounded. Rate Monotonic real-time systems prioritize tasks according to their arrival rate. This paper focuses on the use of the central limit of response times built in \cite{zagalo2022} and an approximation of their distribution with an inverse Gaussian mixture distribution. The distribution parameters and their associated failure rates are estimated through a suitable re-parameterization of the inverse Gaussian distribution and an adapted Expectation-Maximization algorithm. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the method is well-suited for the approximation of failure rates. We discuss the extension of such method to a chi-squared independence test adapted to real-time systems.

papers.title: On a mixed FEM and a FOSLS with $H^{-1}$ loads
papers.abstract: We study variants of the mixed finite element method (mixed FEM) and the first-order system least-squares finite element (FOSLS) for the Poisson problem where we replace the load by a suitable regularization which permits to use $H^{-1}$ loads. We prove that any bounded $H^{-1}$ projector onto piecewise constants can be used to define the regularization and yields quasi-optimality of the lowest-order mixed FEM resp. FOSLS in weaker norms. Examples for the construction of such projectors are given. One is based on the adjoint of a weighted Clément quasi-interpolator. We prove that this Clément operator has second-order approximation properties. For the modified mixed method we show optimal convergence rates of a postprocessed solution under minimal regularity assumptions -- a result not valid for the lowest-order mixed FEM without regularization. Numerical examples conclude this work.

papers.title: A Search-Based Algorithm for Multistage Robust Discrete Linear Optimization and its Implementation
papers.abstract: Robust optimization models that allow decisions to adapt to newly revealed information remain computationally challenging and are often limited to two decision stages or are addressed heuristically or via approximation schemes. This challenge is further amplified when uncertainty sets depend on earlier decisions. Conventional approaches to such problems often require problem-specific reformulations and tailored algorithms, highlighting the need for an exact model-and-run approach. We address this gap by presenting an algorithmic framework for solving multistage robust discrete linear optimization problems. This exact approach adapts and integrates ideas from game-tree search, quantified conflict-driven clause learning, and integer linear programming to explore the minimax tree and is implemented in the open-source solver Yasol. The solver supports discrete decision variables across multiple stages, discrete uncertainty sets with polyhedral or decision-dependent structure, and mixed-integer recourse in the final stage. It can be used as a standalone executable or through a C++ library interface, allowing it to serve as a reference solver for exact methods in multistage robust discrete linear optimization. In an extensive computational study, we demonstrate the capabilities of our solver. The results show competitive performance against a reference approach from the literature for a protection-interdiction problem, as well as strong performance on bilevel benchmark instances. For a multistage cutting-stock problem, we demonstrate the substantial loss in solution quality that can arise from neglecting the multistage structure and show that our solver significantly outperforms decision-rule approximations in terms of computational efficiency while certifying the true multistage optimum.

papers.title: NAG-GS: A Semi-Implicit Stochastic Optimizer with Large-Step Stability
papers.abstract: Stochastic first-order methods are widely used for large-scale optimization and machine learning, where their performance often depends on the learning rate. We study NAG-GS, a stochastic momentum method based on a semi-implicit Gauss--Seidel discretization of a Nesterov-type flow. For strongly convex quadratics, we determine the exact range of stable step sizes for fixed damping and the step size that minimizes the worst-case spectral radius. When the damping equals the strong-convexity parameter, the method recovers the accelerated asymptotic factor $(\sqrtκ-1)/(\sqrtκ+1)$, where $κ$ is the condition number. We also prove that the quadratic iteration converges linearly with dynamic damping when its limiting fixed-damping iteration is stable. For general strongly convex, possibly nonsmooth objectives, we establish an $O(1/k)$ bound on the expected objective gap of the last iterate, using a conditionally unbiased stochastic first-order oracle with bounded second moment. The result holds with dynamic damping from any $γ_0>0$. We show that NAG-GS can also be written as a Heavy-Ball iteration with explicitly determined step sizes and momentum coefficients. We test the stochastic result on nonsmooth hinge-loss classification problems, and further evaluate NAG-GS on quadratic problems, logistic regression, convolutional neural networks, RoBERTa, and Vision Transformers. The experiments show that NAG-GS can remain effective at learning rates where standard optimizers become unstable or lose accuracy.

papers.title: Decay of correlations and thermodynamic limit for the circular Riesz gas
papers.abstract: We study the circular Riesz gas, a one-dimensional system of particles with power-law repulsion. For the long-range gas, we prove that the correlation between two gaps at distance $d$ decays like $d^{s-2}$, up to an arbitrarily small loss in the exponent, and that this exponent is sharp. As a consequence, the microscopic point process converges as the number of particles tends to infinity, and its limit is hyperuniform. We also prove the decay of correlations and the convergence of the microscopic point process for the hypersingular gas. The proof analyzes the Helffer-Sjöstrand equation, an elliptic system in high dimension that encodes covariances. It combines the deformation of Combes and Thomas with discrete elliptic regularity estimates and a factorization around the equally spaced configuration.

papers.title: A model predictive control framework with robust stability guarantees under unbounded disturbances
papers.abstract: To address feasibility issues in model predictive control (MPC), most implementations relax state constraints by using slack variables and adding a penalty to the cost. We propose an alternative strategy: relaxing the initial state constraint with a penalty. Compared to state-of-the-art soft constrained MPC formulations, the proposed formulation has two key features: (i) input-to-state stability and bounds on the cumulative constraint violation for unbounded disturbances; (ii) close-to-optimal performance under nominal operating conditions. The idea is initially presented for open-loop asymptotically stable nonlinear systems by designing the penalty as a Lyapunov function, but we also show how to relax this condition to: i) Lyapunov stable systems; ii) stabilizable systems; and iii) utilizing an implicit characterization of the Lyapunov function. In the special case of linear systems, the proposed MPC formulation reduces to a quadratic program, and the offline design and online computational complexity are only marginally increased compared to a nominal design. Numerical examples demonstrate benefits compared to state-of-the-art soft-constrained MPC formulations.

papers.title: Equating the Area Sums of Alternate Sectors of a Disc Cut by Concurrent Chords
papers.abstract: A disc is cut by $n$ chords through a common interior point $O$, which produces $2n$ curvilinear sectors. We determine when the two sums of alternate sectors have equal area for arbitrary chord directions, which need not be equally spaced. We first derive a closed form for the area of a single sector. We then show that the answer depends on the parity of $n$. For even $n$, at fixed orientation the condition is affine in $r_0^2$, where $r_0$ is the distance from $O$ to the centre; it involves only the total angle of the odd sectors and one trigonometric moment of the directions. For odd $n$, the condition is a nonlinear alternating sum of circular-segment functions of the distances of the chords from the centre. We treat four, six and eight pieces in detail. We also hold the chord directions fixed and translate the whole pencil to an arbitrary interior point, and we characterise the direction sets that give equal sums at every such point. For four chords only equally spaced directions have this property, which gives a converse of the pizza theorem; for an odd number of chords no direction set has it. A fair two-chord cut requires the acute angle between the chords to lie within $(r_0/a)^2$ radians of a right angle, where $a$ is the radius. For equally spaced chords the results reduce to the known theorems of Goldberg and of Mabry and Deiermann.

papers.title: The Hardy-Littlewood conjectures on the twin primes and the binary Goldbach problem are true
papers.abstract: A celebrated conjecture of Hardy and Littlewood provides with an asymptotic formula for the counting function of the twin primes. We give an unconditional proof of such a formula by means of a finite Ramanujan expansion of the counting function expressed in terms of the von Mangoldt function and its incomplete form. In a completely analogous way, we solve the conjugate conjecture on the representations of any even integer as the sum of two prime numbers.

papers.title: Interactive Particle Systems on Hypergraphs, Drift Analysis and the WalkSAT algorithm
papers.abstract: We analyze the expected running time of WalkSAT, a well-known local search procedure for satisfiability solving, on satisfiable instances of the k-XOR SAT problem. We obtain estimates of this expected running time by reducing the problem to a setting amenable to classical techniques from drift analysis. A crucial ingredient of this reduction is the definition of (new, explosive) hypergraph versions of interacting particle systems, notably of coalescing and annihilating random walks as well as the voter model. The use of these tools allows to show that the expected running time of WalkSAT depends on structural parameter (we call odd Cheeger drift) of the dual of the formula hypergraph.

papers.title: Smooth quotients of principally polarized abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We give an explicit characterization of all principally polarized abelian varieties $(A,Θ)$ such that there is a finite subgroup of automorphisms $G$ of $A$ that preserve the numerical class of $Θ$, and such that the quotient variety $A/G$ is smooth. We also give a complete classification of smooth quotients of Jacobians of curves.

papers.title: Enumeration of plane unicuspidal curves of any genus via tropical geometry
papers.abstract: We enumerate complex curves on toric surfaces of any given degree and genus, having a single cusp and nodes as their singularities, and matching appropriately many point constraints. The solution is obtained via tropical enumerative geometry. The same technique applies to enumeration of real plane cuspidal curves: We show that, for any fixed $r\ge1$ and $d\ge2r+3$, there exists a generic real $2r$-dimensional linear family of plane curves of degree $d$ in which the number of real $r$-cuspidal curves is asymptotically comparable with the total number of complex $r$-cuspidal curves in the family, as $d\to\infty$.

papers.title: The double coset problem for parabolic subgroups of braid groups
papers.abstract: We solve the double coset problem for arbitrary parabolic subgroups of the $n$-strand braid group $B_n$, by reducing it to the simultaneous conjugacy problem in the larger group $B_{n+1}$. The resulting decision algorithm is uniform in the braid index and the supplied subgroup generators. We also formulate the reduction for general group embeddings, and apply it to additional commuting constraints, several other spherical Artin types, and finite direct products.

papers.title: Non-collapsing of fibers in warped-product Poincare--Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $g=g_M+u^2h$ be a Poincaré--Einstein (asymptotically hyperbolic Einstein, AHE) metric of class $C^{3,α}$ on $N^{n+1}=M^q\times F^p$, where $(F,h)$ is compact with unit volume and $\Ric_h=λh$, $λ\le 0$. We show that if the conformal infinity $[γ]$ has positive Yamabe constant, then \[ u\;\ge\;Θ[γ]:=\sup_η\Big(\min_{\dN}ψ_η\Big)\Big(\frac{\min_{\dN} s_η}{n(n-1)}\Big)^{1/2}>0, \] the supremum being over representatives $η\in[γ]$ of positive scalar curvature and $ψ_η$ the boundary warping function of $η$. In particular $u\ge (\Y[γ]/n(n-1))^{1/2}\minψ_{η_Y}$ for the Yamabe metric $η_Y$. The estimate rests on a comparison principle between $\ln u$ and Lee's eigenfunction, which also applies to each factor of a multiply warped product, and pointwise yields $u\ge(\minψ_η)\,w_η$ when $\Y[γ]\ge 0$. We give an explicit bound in terms of the product representative of $[γ]$, show that the hypotheses force $q\ge 3$ and $\partial M$ connected, prove lower semicontinuity of $Θ$ in the boundary data, and discuss examples (hyperbolic Fermi coordinates, AdS--Schwarzschild) showing that the hypothesis $λ\le0$ cannot be removed.

papers.title: The View-Obstruction Problem for Spheres in Dimensions Six and Seven
papers.abstract: Place closed Euclidean balls of radius r at the points of (1/2, 1/2, ..., 1/2) + Z^n. The view-obstruction problem for spheres asks for the least r such that every ray from the origin into the open positive orthant meets a ball. Equivalently, it asks for D_n = sup_v min_{t in R} sum_i ||t v_i - 1/2||{Z}^2 over positive integer vectors v, where ||x||{Z} denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer. The values for n <= 5 are classical. We prove D_6 = 107/312, attained only by permutations of (12, 9, 7, 5, 3, 2), and D_7 = 73/180, attained only by permutations of (11, 10, 8, 7, 4, 3, 1). The proof reduces the supremum to a finite search. The key facts are an exact lower bound d_n(v) >= delta^2_U for every rational subspace U perpendicular to v, a matching fiber upper bound, and Banaszczyk's transference theorem, applied along the Korkine-Zolotarev flag of the dual lattice v^perpendicular intersection Z^n. The search is quotiented by signed coordinate permutations and carried out entirely in exact rational arithmetic. It terminates with a certificate: no node of the search is left unresolved, and every surviving candidate is evaluated exactly. The method also recovers the known values for n = 3, 4, 5.

papers.title: Simple Torsion-Free Linear Groups from Global Division Algebras
papers.abstract: We investigate the reduced norm-one group $\mathrm{SL}_1(D)$ of a central division algebra $D$ of odd degree over $\mathbb{Q}$. Using the Brauer-Hasse-Noether theorem and the Margulis-Platonov theorem, we derive a criterion for abstract simplicity in terms of local division completions. For a division algebra of degree $15$ with local invariants $1/3$, $-1/3$, $1/5$, and $-1/5$, the construction yields a candidate example of an infinite, torsion-free, nonabelian simple linear group. This would provide an affirmative answer to Problem 16.78 of the Kourovka Notebook. The argument was generated using an AI system and has not yet been independently verified by human mathematicians.

papers.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in eight dimensions over the field with two elements
papers.abstract: Fuglede's conjecture in a finite abelian group says that a nonempty subset tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral, meaning that the space of complex-valued functions on the subset has an orthogonal basis consisting of restrictions of group characters. We prove the conjecture in the eight-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements. In fact, every spectral set and every tile in this space has a tiling complement which is a linear subspace. We first prove that the Fourier support of a nonempty proper subset of density different from one half contains a two-dimensional subspace. Consequently, every spectral set of density one quarter has a subspace tiling complement. This gives a simpler proof of Kadowaki's dimension-seven result, replacing his use of the classification of Hadamard matrices of order 32 by the classical five classes of order 16. Our dimension-eight proof uses exact finite verifications involving Hadamard matrices of order 32 and perfect codes of length 15. We include the proofs of the reductions used from Kadowaki's preprint, so that neither positive result depends on his dimension-seven theorem. Finally, we give an elementary spectral example of density one eighth in dimension nine whose Fourier support contains no three-dimensional subspace. Thus, the Fourier-support argument at quarter density does not extend in this form to eighth density. Dimension nine is the only case still unresolved over the field with two elements, and this obstruction shows why the present Fourier-support method cannot resolve it as it stands.

papers.title: The inverse Monge--Ampère flow on klt Fano varieties
papers.abstract: We establish the long time existence of the inverse Monge--Ampère flow on a klt $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano variety $X$. We further prove that $X$ admits a Kähler--Einstein metric if and only if the flow converges in $L^1$.

papers.title: Moment representations for generalized Lehmer polynomials
papers.abstract: We represent normalized generalized Lehmer polynomials as moments of a random variable constructed from two independent negative binomial variables and an independent uniform variable. An integral form of their known exponential generating function yields mixtures of uniform distributions and convergent double series. We recover Eulerian polynomial identities and give a probabilistic interpretation of anti-diagonal sums of poly-Bernoulli numbers. We also prove moment determinacy, characterize the Stieltjes parameter range, derive Hankel total non-negativity and log-convexity, and identify the boundary distributions.

papers.title: Almost Periodicity Properties Arising From the Sodin-Yuditskii Theory
papers.abstract: The Kotani-Last problem and the Deift conjecture are two well known statements, which both concern the almost periodicity properties of the functions under consideration, and which have both been disproved in their original formulation, which involves Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity. To contrast these disproofs, and to further elucidate the essence of these two challenging problems, we establish positive results regarding each of them by showing that Weyl almost periodicity can be deduced whenever the Sodin-Yuditskii setup can be implemented. The latter requires that the Schrödinger operator associated with the function in question has purely absolutely continuous spectral measure and a spectrum with finite total gap length and the Parreau-Widom property. We also show that the known examples for which Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity has been shown or suggested to fail in the context of the Deift conjecture are in fact Weyl almost periodic. As a result, an accordingly modified version of the Deift conjecture remains a tantalizing open problem.

papers.title: Degree-one cohomology of metacyclic $2$-groups: a low-bit dichotomy
papers.abstract: We study the subalgebra generated by degree-one mod-$2$ cohomology for metacyclic $2$-groups $G=\langle a,b\mid a^{2^α}=1,\ b^{2^m}=a^c,\ b^{-1}ab=a^r\rangle$ with unique normal forms, where $α,m\ge2$ and $r\equiv-1\pmod4$. Presentation compatibility forces $c=0$ or $2^{α-1}$ and $G^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong C_2\times C_{2^m}$. If $c\equiv0\pmod4$, the degree-one-generated algebra is $\mathbb{F}_2 [x,y]/(y^2,x^2+xy)$, a four-dimensional algebra shared by the four nonmodular types of Aaboun--Zekhnini. The unique exceptional case $α=2$, $c=2$ is modular and has infinite-dimensional degree-one algebra $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y]/(y^2,x^2y)$. The regular algebra is PBW, Koszul, universally Koszul, and strongly Koszul, whereas the modular algebra is not Koszul. We realize the regular algebra by inflation from the common quotient $C_4\rtimes_{-1}C_4$ and identify its quadratic dual with the characteristic-two Jordan plane. For the inversion tower $C_4\rtimes_{-1}C_{2^m}$, we give uniform presentations of the full mod-$2$ cohomology rings and determine the kernels and images of inflation in every degree. Their direct limit yields the continuous cohomology ring of $C_4\rtimes_{-1}\mathbb Z_2$. We also record an arithmetic consequence for Galois groups arising over cyclotomic $\mathbb Z_2$-extensions of real quadratic fields.

papers.title: Exact Generic Exponents of Approximation for the Action of the Integral Special Linear Group on the Torus
papers.abstract: Given an integer $n\ge 2$ and points $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}$ lying in the $n$--dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^n$ equipped with its usual metric denoted by $\left\langle\;\cdot\;\right\rangle$, let \[ τ_n(\mathbf x,\mathbf y) = \sup\left\{ τ\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{there exist infinitely many } H\ge1\text{ for which}\\[1mm] \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-τ} \text{ for some } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z) \end{array} \right\} \] be the Diophantine exponent of asymptotic approximation of $\mathbf{y}$ by the orbit of $\mathbf{x}$ under the action of the integral special linear group $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$. Let also \[ \widehatτ_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right) = \sup\left\{ τ\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{for all but finitely many } H\ge1, \text{ there is } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)\\[1mm] \text{such that } \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-τ} \end{array} \right\} \] denote the corresponding exponent of uniform approximation. The main result of this paper proves that for almost all $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{T}^n$ (with respect to the induced Lebesgue measure), $$\widehatτ_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; τ_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; n-1.$$ This is the first result to establish the exact generic approximation exponents for an action of a lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)$ induced by the standard Euclidean action.

papers.title: Realizing graph automorphisms as geometric symmetries of straight line drawings
papers.abstract: Given a finite graph $G$, we characterize the automorphisms and automorphism groups of $G$ that can be realized as geometric symmetries and symmetry groups of straight line drawings of $G$ in the plane. In doing so, we correct a previous version of this characterization from the literature. As an application, we show that the graphs recently constructed by the first two authors to disprove the Polycirculant Conjecture, which have orders $16{,}464^k$ for each positive integer $k$, are the first known vertex-transitive graphs with no non-trivial realizable geometric symmetries. We also construct infinite families of graphs that exhibit all possible kinds of geometric symmetry.

papers.title: Tropical spin Hurwitz numbers
papers.abstract: We introduce a tropical framework for the study of spin Hurwitz numbers and their completed cycles analogues. We use degeneration techniques to obtain an interpretation of spin Hurwitz numbers via tropical covers. We employ the tropical methods to obtain new closed formulae for spin Hurwitz numbers in special cases. Moreover, we employ Fock space techniques to tropicalise completed cycles spin Hurwitz numbers. Using this, we prove that spin Hurwitz numbers admit a piecewise polynomial structure akin to their classical counterparts. We also derive wall--crossing formulae.

papers.title: Homological lifts of Arnold strangeness
papers.abstract: We construct homological lifts of Arnold's strangeness $\operatorname{St}$ for long and closed plane curves. For long curves, we introduce a new $q$-variable quantization polynomial $\operatorname{St}_q$, an edge state sum, designed for categorification and construct a triply graded homology that recovers $\operatorname{St}_q$. We prove strictness by exhibiting long curves with the same number of crossings and the same $\operatorname{St}_q$ (in particular, the same rotation number and $\operatorname{St}$) that are distinguished by the homology. For closed curves, we introduce a corresponding new polynomial $\operatorname{St}_q$ and construct an edge homology. In this case $\operatorname{St}_q$ is recovered from a signed $q$-character $\operatorname{ch}_q$ defined on the canonical cycles of the homology rather than directly from a graded rank. Again, we exhibit closed curves with the same number of crossings and the same $\operatorname{St}_q$ (in particular, the same rotation number and $\operatorname{St}$) that are distinguished by the homology.

papers.title: Shape optimization under minimal width and constant width constraints
papers.abstract: In this paper we study shape optimization problems for planar convex sets with prescribed minimal width or constant width. We prove that the Reuleaux triangle minimizes torsional rigidity among sets of constant width. We also show that the first Dirichlet-Laplace eigenvalue is maximized by the equilateral triangle under a minimal width constraint and by the Reuleaux triangle under a constant width constraint. The proofs use subsets consisting of a disk and three straight or circular caps. Reflection arguments reduce the study to equilateral configurations, which contain a polygon or a disk polygon depending on one parameter. The same cap constructions give a common proof of the known area, Cheeger and inner parallel area inequalities, and yield sharp bounds for all positive moments of the distance to the boundary. We also prove sharp inequalities for concentric disk intersections and decreasing radial integrals, and compare interaction energies for kernels close to a positive constant. This includes a nonempty interval of positive Riesz exponents. Finally, we investigate whether inclusion monotonicity and Minkowski concavity suffice to obtain these comparisons for other functionals.

papers.title: Outer Lipschitz Geometry of Unions of Tangential Nodal Sets
papers.abstract: In 2000, Birbrair and Fernandes proved that the Hölder Semicomplex of the branches of a germ of a curve with its contact orders is a complete invariant of outer bi-Lipschitz equivalence of definable sets in polynomially bounded o-minimal structures. They also proved a realization theorem for it, i.e., for each Hölder semicomplex $G$, there is a germ of a semialgebraic curve $(X,x_0)$ such that the Hölder Semicomplex of $(X,x_0)$ coincides with $G$. In 2000, Birbrair proposed the problem of finding and characterizing all the Hölder semicomplexes that can be realized as a Hölder Semicomplex of a real analytic curve. Solving this problem in its full generality is a notoriously hard task; however, in this paper, we provide a complete answer to this problem when we restrict it to tangential nodal curves: curves defined as the union of the zero set of a harmonic function and its tangent cone at a fixed point.

papers.title: Metric Diophantine approximation with primes on irrational lines
papers.abstract: Let $c>1$ be irrational. We prove that, for almost every $x>0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there are infinitely many triples $(p,r,s)$, with $p$ and $r$ prime and $s$ an integer, for which \[ 0<px-r<p^{-1/3+\varepsilon},\qquad 0<pcx-s<p^{-1/3+\varepsilon}. \] This improves the exponent $1/5$ in the homogeneous-line case of a theorem of Baier and Ghosh. The arithmetic input is the quantitative prime-counting lower bound in Matomäki's proof concerning primes in shrinking neighborhoods of an irrational rotation. We obtain a local first-moment lower bound by fixing the prime numerator and applying the prime number theorem to the admissible prime denominators. Two Selberg sieve squares, together with explicit trigonometric interval approximations, give a pointwise upper bound whose error tends to zero in $L^1$ after normalization. A truncation and density-point argument then yields the almost-everywhere conclusion.

papers.title: Gross--Prasad conjecture in geometric Langlands
papers.abstract: We prove part of the global Gross--Prasad conjecture for $G = \mathrm{SO}_{n} \times \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ and $H = \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ in the unramified de Rham geometric Langlands setting proposed by Ben-Zvi--Sakellaridis--Venkatesh.

papers.title: Asynchronous Parallel Computation of Lagrangian Bounds for Mixed-Integer Stochastic Programs by Frank-Wolfe Methods within Projective Hedging
papers.abstract: We describe an asynchronous parallel method to calculate Lagrangian bounds for mixed-integer stochastic programming problems. As in some prior work, we use a fully corrective Frank-Wolfe method on subproblems within a decomposition method, eventually optimizing subproblems for individual scenarios over the convex hulls of their integer-feasible vertices. However, instead of using progressive hedging as our decomposition algorithm, we employ an asynchronous projective hedging method. Like our earlier work on projective hedging, our algorithm need only solve a subset of the scenario subproblems at each iteration. Here, we further exploit the capabilities of projective hedging to create a parallel implementation capable of fully asynchronous operation. As we demonstrate empirically, this capability can lead to significant efficiency improvements when the subproblems are solved by Frank-Wolfe and have highly variable solve times.

papers.title: Morse-Maxwell Theory for Directed Acyclic Graph
papers.abstract: The Maxwell graph of a directed acyclic graph is obtained from its iterated basin and hill boundaries. The unweighted counts of extrema at these levels need not satisfy Morse inequalities. We assign multiplicities by the reduced homology of lower and upper order links and retain the vertices with nonzero local homology. The resulting graph preserves both boundary hierarchies, the local groups, and the homology of all sublevel and superlevel order complexes. Its descending and ascending Morse numbers satisfy the weak and strong Morse inequalities over any field. We also construct a Morse chain complex and compute the local groups in several examples. Finally, we consider homology on the original Maxwell graph and prove analogous inequalities for path homology using relative local groups.

papers.title: A convexity theorem for proper Dupin hypersurfaces in spheres
papers.abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a (compact, connected, and embedded) proper Dupin hypersurface in a sphere then, viewing $M$ as a submanifold of the ambient Euclidean space, its orthogonal projection to the normal space at any point is convex. This is a generalization of the convexity theorem of Terng for isoparametric submanifolds in Euclidean spaces.

papers.title: Multi-time-scale Control of Power Systems
papers.abstract: The power grid has been dominated by large synchronous generators and clearly separated control layers. Today, power-electronics energy conversion interfaces are rapidly being deployed calling for another look at system-level control hierarchies. This article examines how multi-time-scale modeling, feedback control, and feedback optimization can help reinterpret the traditional organically grown hierarchy of primary control, automatic generation control, and economic dispatch, and enable new approaches for control of contemporary power systems. Beginning with an overview of power system models and conventional operational practices, the article develops connections to modern control architectures that can coordinate heterogeneous resources, account for operational constraints, and exploit faster actuation without overlooking first-principles physics.

papers.title: Variations of the harmonic entropy and linear drift on negatively curved surfaces
papers.abstract: For closed negatively curved surfaces, we obtain formulas for the derivatives of the harmonic entropy of its geodesic flow and the linear drift of its Brownian motion along conformal deformations. We deduce that the harmonic entropy of the geodesic flow of a closed surface of non-constant negative curvature (resp. linear drift of the Brownian motion on its universal cover) is strictly decreasing (resp. increasing) along the normalized Ricci flow. We also prove that any hyperbolic metric on a surface admits a neighborhood in the space of conformal negatively curved metrics in which the linear drift is greater or equal to the Liouville entropy, with equality if and only if the metric is hyperbolic.

papers.title: Hidden Convexity in Multi-Retailer Cold-Chain Allocation: A Cholesky-Spectral Second-Order Cone Programming Approach
papers.abstract: Several dairy retailers share a refrigerated cold-chain network, each allocating products across heat-sensitivity subgroups to maximize quadratic-fractional efficiency (DEA style). This formulation measures spoilage risk per unit of logistics cost, separating technical from scale efficiency. The single-agent problem is a non-convex fractional QCQP, while the multi-retailer game forms a generalized Nash equilibrium problem (GNEP) with a shared risk-budget constraint, which is generally NP-hard. Governed by the Arrhenius spoilage law, the thermal-risk covariance inherits a rank-one-plus-diagonal structure that unlocks hidden convexity. The authors propose the HSDI (Hidden SOCP Dinkelbach Iteration) algorithm via a joint Cholesky-spectral transform. Key contributions include: 1. Establishing simultaneous diagonalization of without requiring matrix commutativity. 2. Deriving an explicit sufficient condition for exact second-order cone programming (SOCP) relaxation, alongside a closed-form suboptimality bound for inexact regimes. 3. Proving global convergence: the outer Dinkelbach loop converges Q-superlinearly (exact) or R-linearly (inexact), and the coupled variational-equilibrium (VE) iteration converges R-linearly under strong monotonicity, achieving an overall complexity while ensuring Lipschitz stability of the primal-dual pair. Calibrated on Vietnam and US dairy markets, HSDI matches the objective value of multi-start non-linear baselines without random restarts, yielding global optima under exactness. HSDI exhibits an empirical scaling exponent of 0.93 (versus 1.30 for SLSQP), offering a certified polynomial-time framework and a stable shadow price for prioritizing cold-chain investments.

papers.title: A Local Stabilized Isogeometric Formulation with Discontinuous Pressure for Mesh-Conforming and Immersed Analysis of Nearly Incompressible Elasticity
papers.abstract: Nearly incompressible materials arise in soft tissues, elastomers, gels, and other soft solids. Yet, numerical modeling remains challenging because displacement-based formulations can exhibit volumetric locking near incompressibility. Mixed displacement-pressure formulations address this difficulty but require compatible approximation spaces satisfying the inf-sup condition. In mixed formulations, discontinuous pressure spaces are attractive since pressure degrees of freedom can be condensed locally. In high-order isogeometric analysis, however, their Galerkin stability requires pressure-grid coarsening that increases with polynomial degree. Here, we develop a variational multiscale (VMS) stabilized mixed isogeometric formulation that retains this locality while substantially relaxing the restriction. The key observation is that VMS stabilization controls nonconstant elementwise pressure modes and is unconditionally stable with respect to its parameter, provided the elementwise constant pressure component satisfies the inf-sup condition. Consequently, for maximally continuous displacement splines, a pressure grid coarsened by a factor of two satisfies the constant-mode inf-sup criterion independently of polynomial degree. Local condensation then yields a displacement-only system, facilitating use in existing displacement solvers. The formulation is further extended to immersed isogeometric analysis with extended B-splines, pressure-cell aggregation, subdivision-based cut-cell quadrature, and weak enforcement of essential boundary conditions. Discrete inf-sup studies and convergence analyses in the Kirsch and Cook's membrane benchmarks demonstrate stability and show that the immersed treatment preserves mixed stability properties. The proposed framework therefore provides a local, high-order, and robust approach for nearly incompressible problems in mesh-conforming and immersed settings.

papers.title: Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control via Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: The curse of dimensionality associated with solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for the value function remains a key obstacle for real-time optimal feedback control of high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems. This is especially severe in aerospace applications such as relaminarizing unsteady turbulent flows and recovering from aerodynamic stall where nonlinear dynamics play a significant role. We introduce Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control (BASOC), a model reduction framework which seeks to find directions in state space along which the value function is most sensitive, and the distribution of states exhibits maximum variance along optimal trajectories. BASOC leverages trajectory optimization and the Pontryagin minimum principle to obtain state and co-state (value function gradient) data along locally optimal trajectories for constructing state and gradient covariance matrices. Balancing these matrices provides an oblique projection for approximating the value function, which can also be used to construct reduced-order models and surrogate feedback control laws. We show that for linear-quadratic optimal control problems, BASOC becomes equivalent to a snapshot method for initial condition balancing of the optimally controlled closed-loop realization. The framework is demonstrated on a nonlinear three-dimensional system where POD and balanced truncation are known to perform poorly, and on the nonlinear complex Ginzburg-Landau equation to demonstrate feasibility for larger-scale systems.

papers.title: The unknotting problem for surfaces in the 4-sphere
papers.abstract: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a closed, connected, orientable, locally flat PL surface in $S^4$ of genus at least 18 (resp. 19) is TOP (resp. PL) unknotted. We prove analogous results for non-orientable surfaces, and for surfaces in any compact PL 4-manifold. We also show that there is an orientable surface in $S^4$ of genus 18 whose group has unsolvable word problem, and an orientable surface in $S^4$ of genus 40 whose group contains an isomorphic copy of every recursively presented group. Similar results hold for non-orientable surfaces.

papers.title: Dirichlet-Constrained Random Operators and Quenched Reflection Quantum Walks: Tree Spectra and Poisson Criticality at High Degree
papers.abstract: We study spectral limits of random operators whose incident edge weights are coupled by local normalization, and the reflection quantum walks associated with them. At each vertex of a $d$-regular graph, an independent Dirichlet probability vector distributes unit mass among outgoing directions. At fixed degree, the empirical spectral measures of the associated self-adjoint operators converge almost surely on locally tree-like graph sequences. We give a closed-walk formula for every moment of the limiting tree law. Our main result identifies two distinct high-degree scales. After rescaling the deterministic expected root spectral law by $\sqrt d$, a weak limit exists if and only if $dα_d^2$ converges in $[0,\infty]$, where $α_d$ is the Dirichlet parameter. The limits range from a point mass at zero through non-semicircular critical laws to the semicircle law. The critical laws admit a Poisson-tree representation with an explicit Bessel intensity. The extended family, including both endpoint laws, provides a first-Wasserstein approximation uniform over positive Dirichlet parameters. In the regime $dα_d^2\to0$, the rescaled law converges weakly to a point mass although its second moment remains one. Weighting spectral mass by its contribution to this moment and rescaling again reveals a different family of limits, classified by $dα_d$. These limits have explicit Beta-product descriptions. A quantitative comparison transfers the variance-scale classification to the centered and rescaled inherited eigenphases of the quantum walk.

papers.title: Integer points for iterated Weierstrass elliptic functions
papers.abstract: Iterated Weierstrass P functions exhibit relationships between period lattices and the dynamics. We connect the dynamical properties to the occurrence of integer and rational points on associated real elliptic curves. Defining a complex number z to be an integer point if both P(z) and P'(z) are integers, we restrict to P when the lattice is real and its invariants g2 and g3 are integers. We study when an integer point lies in the Fatou set of P and when it lies in the Julia set, and if there is any dynamical significance to this. Applying established results on integer solutions to cubic Diophantine equations to the dynamical properties of iterated elliptic P functions, we show integer points at poles of P lie in the Julia set. Integer points can also occur in the Fatou set of P.

papers.title: AHEAD: Adaptive Neural Acceleration for Large-Scale Linear Programming
papers.abstract: Large-scale linear programs with millions of variables and constraints strain time and memory budgets. First-order methods such as the primal-dual hybrid gradient scale to this regime because they avoid matrix factorizations, but they require many iterations. Learned accelerators can reduce these iterations, yet fewer iterations do not guarantee a shorter solve. Learning inference also takes time, and running the accelerator longer trades solver time for inference time. Existing unrolled accelerators handle this trade-off poorly: each layer processes every variable and constraint, the predicted iterates still need solver refinement, and every instance runs the same layers. We therefore ask: What neural accelerator design achieves end-to-end speedups on large-scale linear programs across sizes and target accuracies? We introduce AHEAD, an accelerator that predicts step sizes for first-order linear programming solvers while keeping their update rules. Its weight-shared predictor reads compact solver statistics and rescales the primal and dual step sizes, so each warm-start iteration stays inexpensive and a short warm-start phase hands the solver a warm start. A learned handoff policy sets the number of warm-start iterations for each instance and target accuracy, after which the solver finishes under its own termination criterion. On packing linear programs with up to $10^7$ variables, AHEAD achieves $6.5$--$11.6\times$ end-to-end speedups over Gurobi's first-order solver from a cold start, including on instances of unseen sizes and distributions. The gains extend to PageRank linear programs and hold across difficulty levels and target accuracies.

papers.title: Growing-time trace fluctuations and self-averaging form factors of Grover walks on random lifts
papers.abstract: We prove a functional central limit theorem for trace statistics of Grover walks on random $N$-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple $d$-regular graph, $d\geq3$. All observations are computed from the same random lift. The squared centred traces, divided by their observation times, have averages converging in probability to a degree-dependent constant. Their partial sums, centred at this constant and divided by the square root of the window length, converge to Brownian motion. For a window of length $M$ beginning at $t\geq1$, it suffices that $M\to\infty$ and $R^4(d-1)^R/N\to0$, where $R=t+M$. The initial time may remain fixed, with no further restriction on $M/t$. Convergence holds jointly with fixed low-degree polynomial trace statistics; their limiting vector is independent of the Brownian motion. For non-bipartite bases, we also identify Gaussian trace limits at fixed time offsets. Under common initial-time normalisation, subtracting a deterministic growth profile gives an explicit Brownian time change when $M/t$ has a finite limit. Bipartite bases retain the same averaged constant and have twice the Brownian variance rate. The proof combines a growing-dimensional Poisson approximation, a uniform bilinear Chebyshev-energy estimate, a time-decaying Poisson--Gaussian coupling, and a Gaussian quadratic-array theorem. Separate moment estimates give expectation-centred versions under an additional sufficient condition.

papers.title: Sheaves on polynomials and polynomial sheaves
papers.abstract: We show that several Dold-Kan type equivalences can be understood as a passage from constructible sheaves on symmetric products (i.e. spaces of polynomials) to polynomial sheaves in the sense of Goodwillie-Weiss calculus, by means of a natural analytic expansion functor. This geometric perspective provides access to standard tools from sheaf theory such as the six functor formalism and $t$-structures. For example, the equivalence between filtered objects and coherent chain complexes in a stable $\infty$-category receives a geometric incarnation as Verdier duality between $!$-sheaves and $*$-cosheaves on an $\infty$-dimensional simplex. As a main application, we obtain an intrinsic geometric explanation for the appearance of vanishing cycle data for perverse sheaves in a paracyclic variant of the Dold--Kan correspondence pioneered by Dwyer and Kan, at the same time lifting their equivalence to stable $\infty$-categories.

papers.title: The Andreadakis conjecture
papers.abstract: For $n\ge2$, let $F_n$ be the free group of rank $n$, and let $\IA(F_n)$ be the group of automorphisms of $F_n$ acting trivially on its abelianization. Two natural filtrations of $\IA(F_n)$ are its lower central series $γ_c(\IA(F_n))$ and the Andreadakis filtration $\mathrm{I}_{c+1}\mathrm{A}(F_n)$, consisting of automorphisms acting trivially on $F_n/γ_{c+1}(F_n)$, $c \geq 1$. Andreadakis conjectured that these filtrations coincide. We disprove this conjecture for every $n\ge3$ and $c\ge4$.

papers.title: Building Mathematical Software -- Lessons from the Development of GAP
papers.abstract: Mathematical software has particular needs that are not all covered by the existing literature on software engineering or algorithm design. This paper looks at some of these aspects, in the concrete context of the computer algebra system GAP. It also studies the potential impact AI systems could have on the development process for mathematical software.

papers.title: Multiplicity One for Unitary Ginzburg--Rallis Models over Local Fields
papers.abstract: We prove multiplicity at most one for the unitary similitude Ginzburg--Rallis model over local fields of characteristic zero, for both the quasi-split and non-quasi-split groups. The theorem holds for all irreducible smooth representations over non-Archimedean fields and all irreducible Casselman--Wallach representations over the real field. We first describe the decomposition into parabolic double cosets and compute the required stabilizers. Over a non-Archimedean field we use character obstructions, localization, and transpose symmetry. Over the real field we use a Casimir identity and explicit normal vectors to prove the corresponding statement for distributions with prescribed infinitesimal character. The Gelfand--Kazhdan criterion and a dualizing involution then give the multiplicity bound.

papers.title: A fractional modular Poincaré--Wirtinger-type inequality in Sobolev spaces with variable exponents
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain and let $p:Ω\to[1,\infty)$ be a measurable, essentially bounded exponent; no regularity of $p$ -- in particular, no log-Hölder continuity -- is assumed. For a general non-negative measurable kernel $\mathcal{K}(x,y)$ admitting a radial bounding function $κ(x,r)$ in the second variable, we establish the fractional modular Poincaré--Wirtinger-type inequality $$ \iint_{Ω\timesΩ}\mathcal{K}(x,y)\,|u(x)-u(y)|^{p(x)} d y\, d x \leqslant C\int_Ωc(x)\left(\int_Ω \frac{|\nabla u(z)|^{p(x)}}{|z-x|^{n-1+θ}}\, d z\right) d x, $$ valid for every $u\in W^{1,1}(Ω)$, in particular every $u\in W^{1,p(\cdot)}(Ω)$, and every $θ\in[0,1)$. Here $$ c(x)=\int_0^{D}r^{n+p(x)-2+θ}κ(x,r)\,d r, $$ $D$ is the diameter of any fixed ball containing $\overlineΩ$, and the constant $C$ depends only on $n,p^+,θ$ and the fixed domain $Ω$. For the fractional kernel $\mathcal{K}(x,y)=|x-y|^{-n-λp(x)}$ we obtain a variable-exponent Gagliardo-modular estimate. The proof replaces the starshaped chain decompositions used there by a combination of a Morrey-type estimate on starshaped domains, a positive-kernel proof of weighted Poincaré inequalities, and one reflection extension for the weights $|z-x|^{-(n-1+θ)}$. The constants are uniform down to exponent $1$, and the inequalities are understood in the extended nonnegative sense when either side is infinite.

papers.title: Complete Expanding Interval Maps are Mixing
papers.abstract: We give a new and elementary\footnote{That is: without functional analysis.} proof that certain smooth, complete, expanding maps from the interval to itself are mixing.

papers.title: Pointwise to global good reduction problems
papers.abstract: Given a smooth proper family of varieties over some $p$-adic field, if (sufficiently many of) the closed fibers have good reduction, does the family as a whole have good reduction? This question is asked and positively answered in recent work of Cadoret-Tamagawa for curves in general, and abelian varieties if the base field has absolute ramification at most $p-1$. In this paper we define a general framework for studying this question, yielding new positive answers for families of K3 surfaces and cubic fourfoulds, again with ramification at most $p-1$. Our strategy is to study several extension properties of moduli spaces and how they transfer under various morphisms. Of particular importance are integral canonical models of Shimura varieties, and whether or not their extension properties are preserved under ramified scalar extension. Additionally, building on earlier counterexamples by Raynaud-Ogus-Gabber and Vasiu-Zink, we show that the ramification assumption is optimal for the result of Cadoret-Tamagawa on families of abelian varieties. This reflects the fact that the extension property of Siegel Shimura varieties no longer holds over a field of absolute ramification at least $p$.

papers.title: Cops and Robbers on Graphs without Long or Short Holes
papers.abstract: In 2019, Sivaraman conjectured that every $P_k$-free graph has cop number at most $k-3$ for $k\geq 5$. Chudnovsky, Norin, Seymour, and Turcotte proved $P_5$-free graphs have cop number at most $2$. For $k\geq 6$ Sivaraman's conjecture remains widely open. There is little evidence to believe Sivaraman's conjecture is optimal, making the discovery of substantially better bounds interesting, even for subclasses of $P_k$-free graphs. We consider this problem for graphs with no long holes, which generalizes $P_k$-free graphs, that also have some forbidden shorter holes. Specifically, we show that for $t\geq 13$, $(C_4,\dots, C_{t}, C_k,C_{k+1},\dots)$-free graphs have cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-2}{\lfloor \frac{t}{4}\rfloor }\rceil+1$. Taking $C_{k-1}$, which has cop number $2$ whenever $k\geq 5$, demonstrates that this bound is tight up to a small constant factor for infinity many pairs $k$ and $t$. The proof relies on showing that in graphs without short holes, the closed neighbourhood of a short induced path can be guarded by $1$ cop, even when these paths are not geodesics. Additionally, for $t\geq 2$ we show that $(C_{t+2},C_{t+3},C_k, C_{k+1},\dots, )$-free graphs have cop number at most $(t-1)\lceil \frac{(k-2)}{t}\rceil$. This show that $(C_4,C_5,C_k,C_{k+1},\dots)$-free graphs have cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-2}{2}\rceil$, extending work by Clow and Meger on $(P_k,\text{claw}, \text{butterfly}, C_4,C_5)$-free graphs to a substantially more general class.

papers.title: Retriangular numbers and affine maps between polygonal numbers
papers.abstract: A positive integer $a$ is called \emph{retriangular} if there is a positive integer $b$ such that $aT+b$ is a triangular number whenever $T$ is. We show that the retriangular numbers are exactly the odd squares greater than $1$, and that for each of them $b$ is unique.
